HOW TO SUBMIT A GRANT APPLICATION?

  1. Complete and submit your application using the online application form. Log in at https://www.palyazat.gov.hu via the "Single sign-on Interface Login" button to access the e-Government (EPTK) system.

A user manual illustrating the use of the Unified Institutional System Interface is available at https://help.fair.gov.hu/node/427.

HOW ARE SUBMITTED GRANT APPLICATIONS EVALUATED?

  1. continuously check the eligibility of applications received in each phase according to the eligibility criteria specified in the call.
  2. submit eligible applications for content evaluation on an ongoing basis.
  3. make grant decision in each phase in order of the scores achieved during the evaluation.

Applicants are advised to monitor announcements and system messages. Notifications about budget monitoring are sent only to businesses that have started completing their grant application.

Details are included in the call for proposals entitled Enhancing the Cybersecurity Capabilities of the Domestic SME Sector, code SSNS-NCC-HU-FSTP-2026. The call can be downloaded from the official website of NCC-HU and from the website https://www.palyazat.gov.hu.

If you have any questions or comments regarding the call for proposals, please contact the NCC-HU customer service at ncc-ih@nbsz.gov.hu.
description:
WHO CAN SUBMIT A GRANT APPLICATION?

Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises may submit grant applications for the call if they:

  1. have at least three closed financial years (each supported by financial statements and covering full 365-day period of operation as a pre-company is not included);
  2. operate in the sectors listed in Annexes 2 or 3 of the Cybersecurity Act

WHAT ACTIVITIES ARE ELIGIBLE FOR SUPPORT?

  1. Acquisition of new equipment and intangible assets resulting in the enhancement of cyber resilience
  2. Centralised endpoint protection solutions (traditional antivirus);
  3. Advanced endpoint protection and incident detection solutions (EDR/XDR);
  4. Perimeter protection solutions (firewall, Web Application Firewall, proxy, VPN gateway);
  5. Network traffic monitoring and intrusion detection solutions (WAF, IDS/IPS, NDR);
  6. Solutions against denial-of-service attacks (Anti-DDoS);
  7. Data backup and recovery solutions (backup/restore);
  8. Centralised log collection solutions (log management);
  9. Advanced log analysis solutions;
  10. Security information and event management solutions (SIEM);
  11. Mobile device management solutions (MDM);
  12. Multi-factor authentication solutions (MFA);
  13. Identity and access a management solutions (IAM);
  14. Data loss prevention solutions (DLP);
  15. Anti-spam and e-mail security solutions;
  16. Governance, risk and compliance management solutions (GRC);
  17. Encryption and key management solutions;
  18. Replacement of hardware or software components that are no longer supported by security update (obsolete hardware/software).
  19. Procurement of Services related to the enhancement of cyber resilience:
  20. Cybersecurity testing and assessment services (vulnerability testing);
  21. Cybersecurity Operations Centre (SOC) services;
  22. Cybersecurity-related training activities;
  23. Subscriptions to cybersecurity training platforms;
  24. Integration of hardware and software tools (system design, implementation, configuration, testing and documentation);
  25. Cybersecurity-related consulting and professional advisory services.

Details are included in the call for tenders!

callTitle: Enhancing the Cybersecurity Capabilities of the Domestic SME Sector (SSNS-NCC-HU-FSTP-2026)
furtherInformation:
The purpose of this call for proposals is to enhance the cybersecurity resilience and risk management capabilities of the domestic SME sector, thereby contributing to the objectives of the European Cybersecurity Industrial, Technology and Research Competence Centre (hereinafter: ECCC) as set out in the Digital Europe Cybersecurity 2025-2027 Work Programme.

Under this call for proposals:

  1. Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) may submit grant applications without territorial restrictions;
  2. Applications must comply with the limitations specified in the call;
  3. Eligible applicants are those operating in the sectors listed in Annexes 2 or 3 of Act LXIX of 2024 on Cyber Security in Hungary.

Call for proposals

  1. Managing authority: NCC-HU;
  2. Funding source: Digital Europe Programme and the Hungarian State budget, through NCC-HU call for proposals DIGITAL-ECCC-2024-DEPLOY-NCC-06;
  3. Evaluation procedure: applications will be evaluated in stages with funding decisions taken in order of the scores achieved within each stage.

Rules and Regulations

The detailed rules on how the NCC-HU manages and uses the are set out in Government Decree No. 474/2025. (XII. 30.) on the detailed rules for the activities of the National Coordination Centre (hereinafter: Government Decree). Applicants are hereby informed that the following documents jointly contain all conditions necessary for preparing and submitting a grant application:

  1. the call for proposals,
  2. the Government Decree,
  3. the General Terms and Conditions (hereinafter: GTC),
  4. the NCC-HU Accounting Guide (hereinafter: Accounting Guide),
  5. the grant application form and its annexes.

The managing authority reserves the right to amend the documents. Any amendments will be published and applicants are requested to regularly monitor the official website of the NCC-HU and on the palyazat.gov.hu for updates.

The managing authority may set stricter requirements in the call for proposals than those laid down in the general rules of the Accounting Guide. In the event of any discrepancy between the provisions of the call for proposals and the general provisions of the Accounting Guide, the provisions of the call for proposals shall prevail.

The financing of activities eligible under this call for proposals shall be considered State aid within the meaning of Article 107(1) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU).

Such aid maybe implemented in compliance with EU competition law under the following categories of aid and applicable rules:

  1. General de minimis aid (EU) Commision Regulation 2023/2832

beneficiaryAdministration:
Phortify Internship (Traineeship) Grants

Under this call, Phortify internships refer to short-term, practice-oriented placements, as foreseen in the Phortify Grant Agreement. They are learning-based activities and do not constitute employment.

The Phortify Internship Grants support both students enrolled in Phortify Master’s Degree Programmes and students who are not enrolled in a Phortify Master’s programme, provided that the internship is Phortify-labelled, aligned with the objectives of the Phortify project, and carried out in accordance with the Phortify Grant Agreement.

Participating partners:

Activer Fiber Systems (AFS):

- https://www.afs-jena.de/

ICFO - The Institute of Photonic Sciences:

- https://www.icfo.eu/

Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e):

- Master of Science in Applied Physics

- Master of Science in Electrical Engineering: track (1) Semicon Devices and track (2) Connected World Technologies

Warsaw University of Technology (WUT):

- Master of Science in Mechatronics

- Master of Science In Photonics

Friedrich Schiller University (FSU):

- Master of Science in Photonics

- Master of Science in Quantum Science & Technology


How to apply for funding

Funding opportunities will be advertised through (1) the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, (2) the official Phortify website (https://phortify.eu/my-phortify/) and (3) the official Phortify partner websites.

Applications for Phortify funding must be submitted via the Phortify website. Applicants are required to consult the dedicated MyPhortify page, where all funding opportunities available under this pilot call are listed together with detailed application instructions and links to the relevant local application forms.

Nationality eligibility

  1. Applicants must be nationals of an EU Member State, an associated country, or a country with which the European Union has an ongoing cooperation agreement under the Digital Europe Programme.
  2. Eligible countries include, inter alia, countries participating in Digital Partnerships, Trade and Technology Councils, digital dialogues, or other forms of ongoing international cooperation with the European Commission in the field of digital technologies.

The authoritative list of eligible countries will be published as part of this call and may be updated in accordance with European Commission guidance.

Eligibility

Under this call, Phortify Internship Grants may be awarded to students belonging to one of the following categories:

Category A – Phortify master degree-seeking students

Students who are enrolled in one of the Phortify Master’s Degree Programmes offered by the consortium universities and who undertake a Phortify-related internship during their period of study.

Category B – Phortify non-degree seeking students participating in Phortify student activities

Students who are not enrolled in a Phortify Master’s Degree Programme but who participate in a Phortify-labelled internship, as foreseen under the Phortify Grant Agreement and implemented under the responsibility of a Phortify partner institution.

In all cases, eligible applicants must be students at the time of the internship, and the internship must:

  1. be directly related to the thematic areas and objectives of the Phortify project;
  2. contribute to the academic and professional development of the student;
  3. be carried out during the student’s period of study;
  4. be implemented under the responsibility of a Phortify partner institution.

Applicants must submit the following documentation:

  1. Latest official academic BSc and MSc (if applicable) transcripts
  2. A Phortify-specific motivation letter, describing the applicant’s motivation for applying for Phortify funding and their alignment with the objectives of the Phortify project
  3. A curriculum vitae (CV)

Applications that fail to meet the minimum eligibility requirements or that do not include the required documentation will be declared ineligible and will not be further evaluated.

Evaluation and selection

The predefined evaluation framework applicable to this call is published on the Phortify website as a dedicated evaluation framework document and applies to all partner institutions.

1. Purpose and Scope

This description defines the evaluation framework applied to applications submitted under the Phortify Internship Grants – Pilot Call.

The framework ensures transparency, equal treatment of applicants, consistency across partner institutions, and alignment with the objectives of the Phortify project, including its Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) principles.

2. Evaluation Principles

The evaluation process is based on the following principles:

  1. Transparency and traceability of decisions
  2. Equal and fair treatment of all applicants
  3. Merit-based selection
  4. Consideration of DEI objectives in line with EU guidance

3. Evaluation Process Overview

The evaluation consists of two sequential stages:

  1. Eligibility verification (pass/fail)
  2. Comparative assessment and ranking

4.  Stage 1 – Eligibility Verification

Applications are checked for compliance with all eligibility requirements defined in the call text. Applicants must submit all required supporting documentation, including academic transcripts, a Phortify-specific motivation letter, and a curriculum vitae (CV).

Applications that fail to meet the eligibility requirements or that do not include the required documentation are declared ineligible and are not further evaluated.

5.   Stage 2 – Comparative Assessment

Eligible applications are assessed comparatively using the criteria below. Each criterion is scored independently on a scale from 0 to 5 points.

Evaluation Criteria

  1. Academic Excellence (0/5): Academic performance, relevance of previous studies, and preparedness for the proposed internship.
  2. Motivation and Alignment with Phortify Objectives (0/5): Quality, coherence, and relevance of the motivation letter, including alignment with Phortify’s educational and societal objectives.
  3. Overall Applicant Profile (0/5): Skills, experience, background, and potential contribution to the Phortify community, as reflected in the CV.

Maximum total score: 15 points.

Ranking and Allocation of Funding

Funding under this call is awarded following a rolling call procedure. Applications may be submitted at any time while the call is open. Applications are evaluated at regular intervals, typically every 2 to 3 months, or earlier if the number of submitted applications or budget availability so requires.

Following each evaluation round, eligible applications are ranked in order of merit, and funding is allocated until the available budget under this call is exhausted. In cases of oversubscription, priority is given to higher-ranked applications. Where applications receive identical or comparable evaluation results, tie-break rules promoting underrepresented groups, including women and students from disadvantaged socio-economic backgrounds, will be applied in line with Phortify DEI objectives.

Selection Committees

Applications are evaluated by local selection committees established by the Phortify partner institutions. Committees apply this evaluation framework consistently and impartially. Members must declare any conflicts of interest and ensure appropriate mitigation measures.

Documentation and transparency

Evaluation outcomes and funding decisions are documented by the partner institutions. Awarded grants are communicated to the Phortify Coordinator. Aggregate data will be reported in accordance with the project’s reporting obligations.

Available funding under this call

Type and duration of financial support

Financial support under this call is provided either as a monthly allowance or as a lump sum, depending on the Phortify partner institution.

Monthly allowances are paid for the actual duration of the internship, subject to partner-specific conditions. Lump-sum grants are not linked to a fixed duration and are intended to contribute to the overall costs associated with the internship, such as travel, accommodation, and subsistence.

AFS:

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 1.200/month for master students

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 800/month for bachelor students

ICFO:

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 600/month for a maximum duration of 6 months

TU/e:

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 2.000 - lump sum not linked to duration

WUT:

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 2.000 - lump sum not linked to duration

FSU:

- Phortify Internship Grant of € 1.500 - lump sum not linked to duration


Financial support may only be used for the activities listed above; no other activities are eligible.
description:
About Phortify

Phortify - Photonics Education Network for Next-Gen Innovation and Digital Skills Excellence for Industry and Society - is dedicated to the Enhancement and Harmonisation of Photonics education and training across Europe. Phortify offers a two-year European Master’s in Photonics Engineering, combining advanced coursework, hands-on laboratory training, and cutting-edge digital skills development, structured mobility windows and industry placements. Students who complete the Phortify track receive an official Phortify Certificate in addition to their Master’s degree. Students can enrol in a Phortify-related master programme at any of the 7 participating universities. In addition, Phortify provides stand-alone modules with harmonised standards for quality assurance and certification, offering high flexibility and mobility for both students and industry professionals. Finally, Phortify organises mentoring programmes for women postdocs and early PIs as well as one-day immersive experience events for prospective students, providing a unique opportunity to explore photonics and its applications.

About the Phortify Funding Framework

Phortify’s Funding Framework aims to widen participation in photonics by supporting students and staff who are traditionally underrepresented in STEM. This includes women and gender minorities, students from low-income or socio-economically disadvantaged backgrounds, first-generation university students, and learners with disabilities or specific support needs. The programme also encourages participation from regions with limited access to advanced higher education, as well as those belonging to cultural or minority groups that may be underrepresented in higher education. By addressing these dimensions of diversity, Phortify helps ensure a more inclusive and equitable community of future photonics professionals. Participants selected for Phortify funding receive financial support for studies and mobility pathways within the participating master programmes, or for mentoring programmes and STEM experience workshops organised by one of the Phortify partners.

results.content: TU Graz GreenChips-EDU Scholarship

beneficiaryAdministration:
GreenChips-EDU Scholarship

1. Purpose of the call


The GreenChips-EDU Project was launched in 2023 with the aim of supporting talents in sustainable semiconductor technologies across Europe. The project seeks to educate students and researchers, equipping them with knowledge that will contribute to eco-friendly chip design, energy-efficient manufacturing, and materials innovation for the future of the EU.

As part of this initiative, TU Graz is pleased to announce a call for applications for scholarships supporting Master’s students enrolled or planning to enroll in the relevant study programmes at TU Graz:

  1. Electrical and Electronics Engineering
  2. Information and Computer Engineering
  3. Biomedical Engineering

The scholarship is intended to provide financial support to students participating in academia-industry collaborations through mobility programmes. The goal is to foster cooperation between academia and industry and enrich the educational experience of students dedicated to advancing sustainable and innovative technologies in the electronics and microelectronics sectors.


2. Type of grants


The eligible expenses outlined in this document must be directly related to international and domestic mobility activities carried out at partner institutions participating in the GreenChips-EDU project. These mobility activities may also take place at industrial partner sites, including those that are not formal project partners, provided they align with the project's objectives and offer meaningful academic or professional engagement. In such cases, the mobility may take the form of professional training, enabling students to gain hands-on experience and develop practical skills within relevant industry settings.

University partner institutions include the following:

Politecnico di Torino (PoliTo) – Italy

Technische Universität Darmstadt (TUDa) – Germany

Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya (UPC) – Spain

Grenoble INP – UGA – France

Universidade de Lisboa (ULisboa) – Portugal

Carinthia University of Applied Sciences (CUAS) – Austria

Industry, SME and research partners include:

INESC ID – Portugal

Joanneum Research – Austria

Infineon Technologies Austria – Austria (and global)

Končar Inem – Croatia

Silicongate LDA – Portugal

Aedvices Consulting – France

RUSZ – Austria

Business Konsens OG – Austria

This funding call offers six distinct types of grants. While students are permitted to apply for multiple grants, the total amount awarded to any individual must not exceed €10,000, regardless of the maximum limits assigned to each grant type. Financial aid may be provided in the form of reimbursement and/or a fixed amount granted in advance. Each type of grant specifies which of these funding methods applies.

The total funding available is €40,000.

Students/applicants must disclose any other scholarships or fellowships they have already been awarded or are currently applying for at the time of submitting their application for this scholarship program. Additionally, they must inform us of any scholarships or fellowships they are granted thereafter.


2.1. Coverage for tuition and registration fees


Only semesters that commence before 30 June 2027 are considered eligible. Funding may be provided for up to a maximum of four consecutive semesters, covering credits taken both at TU Graz and at the mobility destination.

Scope of coverage:

  1. Waiver of Tuition Fees for all first-time enrolled credits, provided they align with the academic path designed for the academic activity
  2. Coverage of any mandatory administrative fees
  3. Coverage of any optional fees, if they align with the goals of the scholarship programme
  4. For students, enrolled in a double degree programme, tuitions and fees occurring at host institution
  5. For students enrolled in a double degree programme, cost related to the issuance of the Master’s Degree certificate at both institutions (TU Graz and host institution)

· Electrical and Electronics Engineering

· Information and Computer Engineering

· Biomedical Engineering

EU Member States or countries associated with the Digital Europe Programme (e.g., countries in the European Economic Area - EEA: Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway - and other nations that have signed association agreements, including those from the Western Balkans and Eastern Europe: Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Turkey, and Ukraine).

4.1 Application method and documentation

Applications may be submitted starting from the day following the publication of the scholarship call.

Applications must be submitted by the following deadlines:

(The scholarship call includes four application rounds to allow for phased evaluation and funding, ensuring the full €40,000 grant is awarded in batches by June 2027.)

Call 1: 15 February 2026, 23:59 (CET)

5.  Selection criteria

The evaluation of the applications will be carried out by the selection committee (Prof. Bernd Deutschmann, Semih Ramazanoglu PhD, Marco Pfeifer, Michael Kleinschuster), which will consider the academic merit of the candidate as well as gender and socioeconomic inequalities in the relevant field of studies, mentioned in section 3.1.

Each application will be assigned a score based on an evaluation system of 35 points structured in 6 blocks:


5.1. (20 points) Academic performance (r1)

Academic performance will be measured in terms of the average grade (g) of a completed Bachelor's Degree (or Master's Degree) that is directly linked to the field of studies specified in section 3.1 or is directly connected to or has a special relevance to the objectives of the GreenChips-EDU project.

The calculation will be made by comparing the average grade (g) of the applicant with the average grade (gavg) obtained by all students who have completed the same Bachelor's or Master's Degree in the previous year. Additional considerations:

In the event that the selection committee does not have this data, the applicant will receive 0 points in this section 5.1.

This information must be certified by the institution where the Bachelor's or Master's Degree was obtained.


5.2. (5 points) Additional academic merits (r2)

This section assesses academic merits beyond those derived from their academic performance. Specifically:

·(+1 point) If the student has completed a Bachelor's or Master's Degree beyond that used for the calculation of r1.

·(+1 point) If the student has received a recognition or award for their academic activity. Honours are not included in this consideration.

·(+1 point) If the student is the author of a publication or poster in a conference or research journal.

a.      (+1 point) If the student demonstrates training in the field of sustainability or green electronics (Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Information and Computer Engineering, Biomedical Engineering).

·(+1 point) If the student has developed projects related to the field of studies mentioned in section 3.1 beyond those required to obtain academic degrees.

·The concepts listed above are considered independently, with r2 being the sum of all those that the student fulfills in accordance with the documentation provided.


5.3. (5 points) Professional experience (r3)

The applicant's work experience in the field of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Information and Computer Engineering, Biomedical Engineering will be valued. Depending on the number of accredited hours, the applicant will receive:

·(1 point) Between 100 hours and 500 hours.

·(2 points) Between 500 hours and 900 hours.

·(3 points) Between 900 hours and 1800 hours.

·(4 points) More than 1800 hours.

Applications that prove work experience in the field of sustainability or green electronics (Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Information and Computer Engineering, Biomedical Engineering) will receive an additional point.


5.4. (2 points) Positive gender discrimination (r4)

Two points will be assigned to female applicants, as a mechanism of positive discrimination that seeks to improve the presence of women in the relevant study and industry field.


5.5. (2 points) Situation of vulnerability (r5)

The applicant may receive 2 points if they can prove that they are in a situation of socioeconomic vulnerability. This accreditation may be based on other grants already granted and that takes this condition into account.

5.6. (1 point) Motivation and alignment with the call (r6)

The student's motivation and the alignment of the application with the objectives of the call will be valued with one point.

Applications will be assessed by a selection (Prof. Bernd Deutschmann, Semih Ramazanoglu PhD, Marco Pfeifer, Michael Kleinschuster). The result will be announced electronically to all candidates.

The GreenChips-EDU Project was launched in 2023 with the aim of supporting talents in sustainable semiconductor technologies across Europe. The project seeks to educate students and researchers, equipping them with knowledge that will contribute to eco-friendly chip design, energy-efficient manufacturing, and materials innovation for the future of the EU.

  2. Information and Computer Engineering
  3. Biomedical Engineering

The evaluation of the applications will be carried out by the selection committee (Prof. Bernd Deutschmann, Semih Ramazanoglu PhD, Marco Pfeifer, Michael Kleinschuster), which will consider the academic merit of the candidate as well as gender and socioeconomic inequalities in the relevant field of studies, mentioned in section 3.1.

Each application will be assigned a score based on an evaluation system of 35 points structured in 6 blocks:


5.1. (20 points) Academic performance (r1)

Academic performance will be measured in terms of the average grade (g) of a completed Bachelor's Degree (or Master's Degree) that is directly linked to the field of studies specified in section 3.1 or is directly connected to or has a special relevance to the objectives of the GreenChips-EDU project.

The calculation will be made by comparing the average grade (g) of the applicant with the average grade (gavg) obtained by all students who have completed the same Bachelor's or Master's Degree in the previous year. Students who have completed a Bachelor's programme or Master’s programme at another university (none TU Graz) are required to provide the average grade (gavg) obtained by all students who completed the same Bachelor's or Master's degree at that university in the previous academic year.

Additional considerations:

In the event that the selection committee does not have this data, the applicant will receive 0 points in this section 5.1.

This information must be certified by the institution where the Bachelor's or Master's Degree was obtained.


5.2. (5 points) Additional academic merits (r2)

This section assesses academic merits beyond those derived from their academic performance. Specifically:

·(+1 point) If the student has completed a Bachelor's or Master's Degree beyond that used for the calculation of r1.

·(+1 point) If the student has received a recognition or award for their academic activity. Honours are not included in this consideration.

·(+1 point) If the student is the author of a publication or poster in a conference or research journal.

a.      (+1 point) If the student demonstrates training in the field of sustainability or green electronics (Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Information and Computer Engineering, Biomedical Engineering).

·(+1 point) If the student has developed projects related to the field of studies mentioned in section 3.1 beyond those required to obtain academic degrees.

·The concepts listed above are considered independently, with r2 being the sum of all those that the student fulfills in accordance with the documentation provided.


5.3. (5 points) Professional experience (r3)

The applicant's work experience in the field of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Information and Computer Engineering, Biomedical Engineering will be valued. Depending on the number of accredited hours, the applicant will receive:

·(1 point) Between 100 hours and 500 hours.

·(2 points) Between 500 hours and 900 hours.

·(3 points) Between 900 hours and 1800 hours.

·(4 points) More than 1800 hours.

Applications that prove work experience in the field of sustainability or green electronics (Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Information and Computer Engineering, Biomedical Engineering) will receive an additional point.


5.4. (2 points) Positive gender discrimination (r4)

Two points will be assigned to female applicants, as a mechanism of positive discrimination that seeks to improve the presence of women in the relevant study and industry field.


5.5. (2 points) Situation of vulnerability (r5)

The applicant may receive 2 points if they can prove that they are in a situation of socioeconomic vulnerability. This accreditation may be based on other grants already granted and that takes this condition into account.

5.6. (1 point) Motivation and alignment with the call (r6)

The student's motivation and the alignment of the application with the objectives of the call will be valued with one point.


Resolution of applications

Applications will be assessed by a selection (Prof. Bernd Deutschmann, Semih Ramazanoglu PhD, Marco Pfeifer, Michael Kleinschuster). The result will be announced electronically to all candidates.


6.  Final Report

Students will be asked to provide a final report that outlines the experience and the main outcomes taken from it. This final report aims to help improve the scholarship program and support dissemination by sharing experiences that may inspire other students to participate. Therefore, the following elements are expected as part of the final report:

· A short questionnaire to gather students’ feedback on the scholarship call, aimed at improving future editions.

· A brief video (30 to 60 seconds) focused on the activity funded by the scholarship. This material will be used in outreach campaigns to engage more students and help ensure that the goals of the GreenChips-EDU project continue beyond its official duration.

results.content: Innovation Funding for Estonian Cybersecurity Companies for developing innovative, high value-added products and services

beneficiaryAdministration:
To apply, the following requirements must be met:

  1. The applicant is a company registered in the Estonian Commercial Register.
  2. The company’s business activity is related to cybersecurity products and/or services.
  3. The applicant’s principal activity falls under EMTAK 2025 Division K, including:
  4. Telecommunications
  5. Computer programming
  6. IT consulting
  7. Computing infrastructure and other information service activities
  8. The company’s EMTAK code must be compatible with the scope of the support scheme
  9. The project must involve at least one partner, such as a research or development institution
  10. All project activities must take place within the EU or EEA (EU Member States, Norway, Iceland, or Liechtenstein)
  11. Both the applicant company and the entity controlling the project partner must be registered in the EU or EEA.

To apply, the following steps must be completed:

  1. Identify a suitable research or development partner - Find a research or development institution that matches your project idea
  2. Discuss the project idea with the partner - Agree on the project scope, objectives, expected results, and roles
  3. Request a price quote - Obtain a formal price offer from the research or development institution for their planned work
  4. Prepare the project plan - Describe the project objectives, activities, timeline, budget, and expected impact
  5. Complete the application form - Fill in the required information in the E-grant self-service environment
  6. Submit the application and supporting documents - Upload the project plan, price offer, and all other required documents in E-grant and submit the application.
description: The grant will help strengthen cooperation between research and development institutions and companies or organisations involved in the development of cybersecurity products and services, in order to carry out innovation and development activities in the field of cybersecurity.

A company may apply for support in the amount of €60,000 to €100,000 of the total cost of the product development project. The grant amounts to 70% of the total project costs for micro and small enterprises, 60% for medium-sized enterprises, and 50% for large enterprises.

The grant is targeted at projects carrying out innovation and development activities in the following areas:

  1. cybersecurity automation
  2. the use of artificial intelligence in cybersecurity
  3. tools and strategies for the transition to quantum-resistant cryptographic algorithms
  4. cybersecurity of space technologies

The call deadline of 2 December 2026, may be extended depending on the availability of funding.

Further information on the Innovation Funding is provided by RIA (Estonian Information System Authority) and EIS (Estonian Business and Innovation Agency) websites.

results.content: RESIST II PROCESS INNOVATION OPEN CALL

beneficiaryAdministration:
This open call aims to support European SMEs operating in the Mobility, Transport and Automotive ecosystem to redefine their manufacturing or industrial processes, carrying out improvements in current operations and/or incorporating new methods or systems which allow them to be more digital, green and resilient. The call is split into two cut-offs or application periods: the 1st one, launched on the 13th May 2026, will be opened for 2 months, while the 2nd one is expected to be launched in May 2027

Eligible candidates

The Open call is addressed to SMEs working in the MTA ecosystem and located in EU Member States or SMP associated countries. SMEs can apply individually or in consortium (2-3 SMEs from different NUTS2 regions)

Submission process

Applications to the RESIST II process innovation open call must be submitted electronically vía the following online platform. Eligible candidates must fill in the corresponding application form and upload the required annexes (resilience check + declaration of honour)

Evaluation process in three stages

  1. Verification of the admissibility and eligibility of applications
  2. Analysis of eligible proposals by at least 3 independent experts and scoring according to the 4 evaluation criteria specified in the Guide for applicants. Applications will then be ranked in descending order based on the scores obtained and the established tie-breaking rules
  3. The resulting ranking list must be reviewed by the consortium partners for its validation

results.summary: G INP-UGA GreenChips-EDU Scholarship
results.content: G INP-UGA GreenChips-EDU Scholarship

beneficiaryAdministration:
GreenChips-EDU Scholarship


1.Purpose of the call


The GreenChips-EDU Project was launched in 2023 with the aim of nurturing talent in sustainable semiconductor technologies across Europe. The project seeks to educate students and researchers, equipping them with the knowledge needed for eco-friendly chip design, energy-efficient manufacturing, and innovative materials for the future of the EU.

As part of this initiative, Grenoble INP-UGA is pleased to announce a call for applications for scholarships to support Master’s students enrolled in, or planning to enrol in, relevant study programmes at Grenoble INP-UGA.

These scholarships are intended to provide financial support to students participating in academic collaborations through mobility programmes. The goal is to foster international cooperation and enrich the educational experience of students dedicated to advancing sustainable and innovative technologies in the electronics and microelectronics sectors.


2. Type of grants


The eligible expenses outlined in this document must be directly related to international mobility activities carried out at partner institutions participating in the GreenChips-EDU project. These mobility activities may also take place at industrial partner sites, including those that are not formal project partners, provided they align with the project's objectives and offer meaningful academic or professional engagement. In the field of sustainable electronics, for example, the mobility may take the form of professional training, enabling students to gain hands-on experience and develop practical skills within relevant industry settings.

GreenChips-EDU university partner institutions include the following;

Politecnico di Torino (PoliTo) – Italy

Technische Universität Darmstadt (TUDa) – Germany

Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya (UPC) – Spain

Graz University of Technology – TU Graz – Austria

Universidade de Lisboa (ULisboa) – Portugal

Carinthia University of Applied Sciences (CUAS) – Austria


GreenChips-EDU industry, SME and research partners include:

INESC ID – Portugal

Joanneum Research – Austria

Infineon Technologies Austria – Austria (and global)

Končar Inem – Croatia

Silicongate LDA – Portugal

Aedvices Consulting – France

RUSZ – Austria

Business Konsens OG – Austria

This funding call offers distinct types of grants. While students are permitted to apply for multiple grants, the total amount awarded to any individual must not exceed €5,000 regardless of the maximum limit assigned to each grant type. Financial aid may be provided in the form of reimbursement and/or a fixed amount granted in advance provided supporting documents are submitted.

The total funding available is €40,000

Only activities in related fields that end before 30 September 2027 are considered eligible.

Applications must be submitted by the following deadlines:

· 15 February 2026 23:59 (Brussels time)

· 1 July 2026 23:59 (Brussels time)

· 14 February 2027 23:59 (Brussels time)

· 1 June 2027 23:59 (Brussels time)


2.1. Coverage for internship fees

The grant will reimburse the beneficiary for the actual costs incurred, provided supporting documents are presented.

Scope of coverage:

· Transportation to and from the mobility destination.

· Living accommodation (rent).

2.2. Contribution to the costs of short-term mobility stays related to the Master's Degree

This grant type covers short-term mobility expenses that are not funded by the Erasmus+ Programme. Participation in Blended Intensive Programmes (BIPs) is specifically excluded.

Scope of Coverage:

The mobility period must typically be less than two months. The proposed activity must fall under one of the following eligible categories:

· Participation in international events, such as summer schools, workshops, or conferences.

· Courses beyond those offered by the partners, such as specialization courses, introductory training related to topics addressed in the Master’s thesis, or similar initiatives in the GreenChips-EDU thematic areas.

· Micro-credentials are also eligible for funding under the scholarship programme.

· Completion of a Master’s thesis at a foreign institution that is part of the GreenChips-EDU network.

· Professional training or internships at companies aligned with the GreenChips-EDU project.

Interactive formats offered by the GreenChips-EDU project can be found here: https://www.tugraz.at/projekte/greenchips-edu/news-events/event-calendar

Please find internship opportunities by the GreenChips-EDU project here: https://www.tugraz.at/projekte/greenchips-edu/student-opportunities/internship-offers

Covered Expenses:

Transport and accommodations.

2.3. Contribution to the expenses of long-term mobility stays related to the Master's Degree

This grant type provides additional financial support to ease the financial burden on students participating in long-term mobility programmes, particularly in double degree programmes.

Scope of Coverage:

The GreenChips-EDU programme may cover days that exceed the maximum Erasmus+ funded duration (e.g., a 6-month stay with only 5 months of Erasmus+ support).

For students enrolled in a double degree programme, GreenChips-EDU may provide living support during the first year of the programme while the students are at Grenoble INP-UGA .

Covered Expenses:

Transport and accommodation.

2.4. Contribution to expenses for scientific achievements during the mobility stay

This grant type supports research activities carried out by Master’s students working on their final projects, ideally during a period of mobility, which lead to a scientific publication aligned with GreenChips-EDU topics. All expenses must be incurred before 30 September 2027.

Scope of Coverage:

Scientific Publication Fees:

Up to €1,000 for full open-access publication in Q1 or Q2 journals.

Up to €500 for full open-access publication in Q3 or Q4 journals.

Presentation Materials:

Up to €100 for preparing posters for scientific congresses.

High-Level Conference Attendance:

Up to €1,500 for registration, travel and accommodation.

3. Who can apply for this grant?


3.1 Applicants criteria


To be eligible for the grant, applicants must meet all of the following conditions:

The student/applicant must be enrolled in an appropriate programme of study at Grenoble INP-UGA (Nanotech or SEI) or be pursuing a double degree programme that correlates with the project topics. They must also have applied for admission for the 2025/26 academic year or later.

The applicant must hold the nationality of:

EU Member States or countries associated with the Digital Europe Programme (e.g., countries in the European Economic Area - EEA: Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway - and other nations that have signed association agreements, including those from the Western Balkans and Eastern Europe: Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Turkey, and Ukraine).


4. Submission of applications

4.1 Application method and documentation

Applications can be submitted from the day after the scholarship call is published. Submissions will be accepted within the designated deadline (see deadlines or at the latest, until 1 June, 2027).

Applications must be submitted to the designated office at Grenoble INP-UGA. For applications or enquiries, please email panagiota.morfouli@grenoble-inp.fr.

Applications will be examined and evaluated by a committee comprising Panagiota MORFOULI, Clemens WINKELMANN, Cyrille CHAVET and Laurent MONTES.

The following documentation must be attached to the application form:

Cover Letter (Form A):

· Please submit a cover letter including the following: A brief introduction of yourself, highlighting your academic background / merits and current field of study. A description of your personal, social, economic, and professional circumstances, as well as your academic performance, that may be relevant to your scholarship application. If possible, please outline your future academic and career plans, including the field in which you wish to further pursue your academic studies.


Type of Grant (Form B) (see checklist below):

· Indicate the type(s) of grant you are applying for. Multiple selections are allowed if you are applying for more than one type.


Academic Grade Documentation:

· Please provide a document stating the average grade of your completed Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree in a field with a strong relevance to the objectives of the GreenChips-EDU project. (See Section 3.1)

The selection committee will check the average grades of all students on the same degree programme over the past year and use them as part of the selection criteria.

Documentary accreditation:

Applicants are responsible for providing supporting documentation for the situations described in the previous point, which are likely to refer to eligibility criteria or merit-based considerations. This includes:

· Documentation required for GPA and academic merits

You should provide the following:

o Official academic transcripts from your institution(s);

o Degree certificates or diplomas;

o GPA certification or a document explaining the grading scale (especially if it is not standard);

o Letters of recommendation (if applicable);

o Documentation for social and economic circumstances.

You may need to submit the following:

o Proof of income (e.g., tax returns, salary slips, or income certificates);

o Family income statements or affidavits;

o Social security or welfare documentation;

o Proof of residence in a disadvantaged area (if relevant);

o Medical or disability certificates (if applicable);

o Any official documentation supporting claims of economic hardship or social disadvantage.

· Accreditation of Mobility Placement

Applicants must provide:

o Proof that they have secured a mobility placement in one of the destinations approved by the call. If this has not yet been confirmed, they must provide a document signed by the Head of Studies of their institution and the Deputy Director of International Relations, endorsing the application.

This document must clearly state the destination of the mobility placement and the estimated length of time that the student will be abroad.


· Justification for Grants Type 2.2 – Short-term mobility stays

Applicants must submit a document justifying the relevance and benefits of the specialized training. This document must include the following:

o The name and description of the course or activity;

o Its purpose;

o The organizing institution;

o The location where the training takes place;

o Course registration confirmation or payment confirmation (if applicable).


· Documentation for Grants Type 2.4 – Scientific Achievement

Applicants must provide:

o A copy of the publication or poster related to the grant application;

o The complete reference number of the place of publication;

o All documentation to verify the publication-related expenses.


5. Selection criteria

The selection committee will evaluate the applications, considering the academic merit of the candidates, as well as gender and socioeconomic inequalities in the field of electronic engineering.

Each application will be assigned a score based on a 20-points evaluation system structured into six blocks:


5.1. (10 points) Academic performance (r1)

Academic performance will be measured in terms of the average grade (g) obtained for a completed Bachelor's or Master's Degree in electronic engineering or a subject directly connected to, or of special relevance to, the objectives of the GreenChips-EDU project.

This will be calculated by comparing the applicant’s average grade (g) with the average grade (gavg) obtained by all students who completed the same Degree the previous year.


Additional considerations:

Applicants are solely responsible for providing their grade point average (GPA). If the selection committee does not have this data, the application will receive 0 points in this section.

This information must be certified by the institution where the Degree was obtained.


5.2. (2 points) Additional academic merits (r2)

This section considers academic merits that go beyond academic performance. Specifically:

  1. (+1 point) If the student has received training in the field of sustainability or green electronics.
  2. (+1 point) If the student has developed projects related to electronics beyond what was required to obtain the academic degrees.  

The above concepts are considered independently, with r2 being the sum of all those that the student fulfills, in accordance with the provide documentation.


5.3. (2 points) Additional academic merits (r2)


The applicant's work experience in the field of electronic engineering will be valued. Depending on the number of accredited hours, the applicant will receive:


   (0.5 point) Between 100 hours and 500 hours.

   (1 points) Between 500 hours and 900 hours.

   (1.5 points) Between 900 hours and 1800 hours.

   (2 points) For more than 1800 hours.


Applications that demonstrate relevant work experience in the field of sustainability or green electronics will receive an additional point.

5.3. (2 points) Positive gender discrimination (r2)

Two points will be awarded to female applicants, as a form of positive discrimination to improve the representation of women on the Bachelor’s or Master's Degree programme.

5.4. (2 points) Situation of vulnerability (r3)

The applicant may receive two points if they can prove that they are experiencing socioeconomic vulnerability. This accreditation may be based on grants that have already awarded and take this condition into account.

5.5. (2 point) Motivation and alignment with the call (r4)

The student's motivation and how well the application aligns with the objectives of the call will be valued at one point.


Resolution of applications

Applications will be assessed by a selection committee.

The result will be announced electronically to all candidates.

These scholarships are intended to provide financial support to students participating in academic collaborations through mobility programmes. The goal is to foster international cooperation and enrich the educational experience of students dedicated to advancing sustainable and innovative technologies in the electronics and microelectronics sectors.


2. Type of grants


The eligible expenses outlined in this document must be directly related to international mobility activities carried out at partner institutions participating in the GreenChips-EDU project. These mobility activities may also take place at industrial partner sites, including those that are not formal project partners, provided they align with the project's objectives and offer meaningful academic or professional engagement. In the field of sustainable electronics, for example, the mobility may take the form of professional training, enabling students to gain hands-on experience and develop practical skills within relevant industry settings.

GreenChips-EDU university partner institutions include the following;

Politecnico di Torino (PoliTo) – Italy

Technische Universität Darmstadt (TUDa) – Germany

Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya (UPC) – Spain

Graz University of Technology – TU Graz – Austria

Universidade de Lisboa (ULisboa) – Portugal

Carinthia University of Applied Sciences (CUAS) – Austria

The mobility period must typically be less than two months. The proposed activity must fall under one of the following eligible categories:

· Participation in international events, such as summer schools, workshops, or conferences.

· Micro-credentials are also eligible for funding under the scholarship programme.

Transport and accommodation.

Presentation Materials:

Up to €100 for preparing posters for scientific congresses.

Up to €1,500 for registration, travel and accommodation.

description:
This support package is meant to facilitate MSc students in fusion who want to go abroad for an internship, thereby stimulating quality of education through exchanges. The internship can take place at a fusion research centre or university involved in fusion research. This place is not limited to Europe. Students registered at universities that are a FuseNet member and/or are doing their internship at hosts that are a FuseNet member, and their home university is located in one of the EUROfusion member states can apply for financial support for their internship here.

The financial support consists of a fixed amount of travel support (depending on the travel distance) and accommodation/living support (depending on the internship duration). The application has to be submitted at least 2 weeks before and within 6 months of the start of the internship. Other sources of funding for the internship (scholarships or grants, compensation or salary from the host institute, funds from other EU support schemes, etc.) need to be specified. Funding can also be restricted in cases where funding has been received from FuseNet in the past (see the terms and conditions on the FuseNet webpage).

• Relevance to programme objectives;

GreenChips-EDU Scholarship

1. Purpose of the call

The GreenChips-EDU Project was launched in 2023 with the aim of supporting talents in sustainable semiconductor technologies across Europe. The project seeks to educate students and researchers, equipping them with knowledge that will contribute to eco-friendly chip design, energy-efficient manufacturing, and materials innovation for the future of the EU.

As part of this initiative, TU Darmstadt is pleased to announce a call for applications for scholarships supporting Master’s students enrolled or planning to enrol in the relevant study programmes at TU Darmstadt:

· Electrical Engineering and Information Technologies

· Information and Communication Engineering

· Information Systems Engineering

These scholarships are intended to provide financial support to students participating in academia-industry collaborations through mobility programmes. The goal is to foster international cooperation and enrich the educational experience of students dedicated to advancing sustainable and innovative technologies in the electronics and microelectronics sectors.

2. Type of grants

The eligible expenses outlined in this document must be directly related to international and domestic mobility activities carried out at partner institutions participating in the GreenChips-EDU project. These mobility activities may also take place at industrial partner sites, including those that are not formal project partners, provided they align with the project's objectives and offer meaningful academic or professional engagement. In such cases, the mobility may take the form of professional training, enabling students to gain hands-on experience and develop practical skills within relevant industry settings.

University partner institutions include the following:

Politecnico di Torino (PoliTo) – Italy

Technische Universität Graz (TUG) – Austria

Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya (UPC) – Spain

Grenoble INP – UGA – France

Universidade de Lisboa (ULisboa) – Portugal

Carinthia University of Applied Sciences (CUAS) – Austria

Industry, SME and research partners include:

INESC ID – Portugal

Joanneum Research – Austria

Infineon Technologies Austria – Austria (and global)

Končar Inem – Croatia

Silicongate LDA – Portugal

Aedvices Consulting – France

RUSZ – Austria

Business Konsens OG – Austria


This funding call offers six distinct types of grants. While students are permitted to apply for multiple grants, the total amount awarded to any individual must not exceed €10,000, regardless of the maximum limits assigned to each grant type. Financial aid may be provided in the form of reimbursement and/or a fixed amount granted in advance. Each type of grant specifies which of these funding methods applies.

The total funding available is €40,000.

Students/applicants must disclose any other scholarships or fellowships they have already been awarded or are currently applying for at the time of submitting their application for this scholarship program. Additionally, they must inform us of any scholarships or fellowships they are granted thereafter.

2.1. Coverage for tuition and registration fees

Only semesters that commence before 30 June 2027 are considered eligible. Funding may be provided for up to a maximum of four consecutive semesters, covering credits taken both at TU Darmstadt and at the mobility destination.

Scope of coverage:

· Waiver of Tuition Fees for all first-time enrolled credits, provided they align with the academic path designed for the academic activity

· Coverage of any mandatory administrative fees

· Coverage of any optional fees, if they align with the goals of the scholarship programme

· For students, enrolled in a double degree programme, tuitions and fees occurring at host institution

· For students enrolled in a double degree programme, cost related to the issuance of the Master’s Degree certificate at both institutions (TU Darmstadt and host institution)

Funding Limit:

Under this grant type, each beneficiary may receive a maximum of €3,500 as reimbursement.

2.2. Coverage for participating specialized courses/trainings

This grant type supports participation in specialization courses or training programmes offered by universities or industries affiliated with the GreenChips-EDU project. It is intended to complement international and domestic mobility activities. All expenses must be incurred before 30 June 2027.

Scope of coverage:

These expenses are related to activities additional to those initially agreed upon for the mobility period. Examples of concepts that could be covered by the programme include:

· Courses beyond those offered by the TU Darmstadt degree programme, such as specialization courses, introductory training related to topics addressed in the Master’s thesis, or similar initiatives in the GreenChips-EDU thematic areas, are also eligible.

· Micro-credentials are also eligible for funding under the scholarship programme.

Covered Expenses:

Registration or tuition fees for extra courses, certification costs for micro-credentials, Material or software required for those additional courses, travel or accommodation if the course or training is held at a different location (if justified).

Funding Limit:

Under this grant type, each beneficiary may receive up to €1,500 as reimbursement. The grant type 2.2 grant includes a travel allowance of max. 500 €, including a daily scholarship rate (ranging from 5 -15 €, depending on the host country), and reimbursement of the course fees, up to a maximum of 1000 €.

2.3. Coverage for the costs of issuing documentation

This grant type covers essential expenses related to obtaining the documentation required by the host institution, provided these are necessary for international mobility. All expenses must be incurred before 30 June 2027.

Covered Expenses:

· Visa & Residence Permit Application and Issuance

– Costs associated with applying for and obtaining a visa/ residence permit.

·Insurance Coverage

– Expenses for life, health, accident, and civil liability insurance required during the mobility period.

· Language Accreditation

– Fees for language proficiency exams and official language certificates.

· Translation fees

– Costs for translations of required documents.

Funding Limit:

Under this grant type, each beneficiary may receive up to €1,000 as reimbursement.


2.4. Contribution to the costs of short-term mobility stays related to the Master's Degree

This grant type supports short-term mobility expenses not covered by the Erasmus+ Programme. It specifically excludes participation in Blended Intensive Programmes (BIPs).

The applicant may receive 2 points if they can prove that they are in a situation of socioeconomic vulnerability. This accreditation may be based on other grants already granted and that takes this condition into account.

The student's motivation and the alignment of the application with the objectives of the call will be valued with one point.

1. Purpose of the call

The GreenChips-EDU Project was launched in 2023 with the aim of supporting talents in sustainable semiconductor technologies across Europe. The project seeks to educate students and researchers, equipping them with knowledge that will contribute to eco-friendly chip design, energy-efficient manufacturing, and materials innovation for the future of the EU.

As part of this initiative, TU Darmstadt is pleased to announce a call for applications for scholarships supporting Master’s students enrolled or planning to enrol in the relevant study programmes at TU Darmstadt:

· Electrical Engineering and Information Technologies

· Information and Communication Engineering

· Information Systems Engineering

These scholarships are intended to provide financial support to students participating in academia-industry collaborations through mobility programmes. The goal is to foster international cooperation and enrich the educational experience of students dedicated to advancing sustainable and innovative technologies in the electronics and microelectronics sectors.

2. Type of grants

The eligible expenses outlined in this document must be directly related to international and domestic mobility activities carried out at partner institutions participating in the GreenChips-EDU project. These mobility activities may also take place at industrial partner sites, including those that are not formal project partners, provided they align with the project's objectives and offer meaningful academic or professional engagement. In such cases, the mobility may take the form of professional training, enabling students to gain hands-on experience and develop practical skills within relevant industry settings.

University partner institutions include the following:

Politecnico di Torino (PoliTo) – Italy

Technische Universität Graz (TUG) – Austria

Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya (UPC) – Spain

Grenoble INP – UGA – France

Universidade de Lisboa (ULisboa) – Portugal

Carinthia University of Applied Sciences (CUAS) – Austria

Industry, SME and research partners include:

INESC ID – Portugal

Joanneum Research – Austria

Infineon Technologies Austria – Austria (and global)

Končar Inem – Croatia

Silicongate LDA – Portugal

Aedvices Consulting – France

RUSZ – Austria

Business Konsens OG – Austria

results.content: Call for proposal for support to Slovenian and Croatian SCOs to “Go out and vote!” campaigns

beneficiaryAdministration:
Purpose of the call: to provide support to Go out and vote! Campaigns that motivate people to vote for defence of EU values (in Slovenia and Croatia)

Expected results (apply to both countries):

-strengthened civil society watchdog/advocacy role (Increased involvement of CSOs in monitoring of political promises; increased number of CSOs mobilizing citizens in civic activities; increased number of CSOs engaged in civic education; increased number of monitoring tools)

-Increased promotion and public awareness of EU rights and values (increased number of awareness raising actions/campaigns)

Increased civic engagement in environmental protection/climate change (support to innovative methods for the protection of the environment; support for the awareness raising actions/campaigns.)

Submission and evaluation process (apply to both countries):

The call is an open-end call for proposals which will remain open until the budget is exhausted, or until 01/01/2028 at the latest. Applications with the required attachments must be submitted exclusively in electronic form to the designated email address: Croatia – akcije.cerv@zaklada-slagalica.hr; Slovenia - akcije.cerv2@cnvos.si. These email addresses are intended solely for the submission of applications for this Call and will not be monitored before the beginning of the application acceptance date. Applications submitted sooner or in any other way (e.g., by fax, regular mail, etc.) or sent to another email address will be rejected.

Applications must be delivered to the specified email address no sooner than November 5, 2025. Applications delivered to the specified email address before this date will be rejected. The date and time of email delivery with the completed application and all required attachments are those recorded on the server of CNVOS/Community Foundation Slagalica.

After submitting application, applicants will receive an automatic response to the email address from which the application was sent. If such a response does not arrive in the applicant's email inbox or spam folder within two (2) hours after sending the application, applicants may contact CNVOS or CFS during the publicised office hours for check of the application status.

  1. A complete application includes:

● A fully completed application form (Word),

● A fully completed financial plan (Excel),

● A completed form with applicant and project details (Excel),

● A scanned, signed, and stamped Applicant's Statement declaring they accept the conditions of the call, including the compliance with the EU values (in .pdf format),

● A scanned, signed (and stamped) Partner's Statement declaring they accept the conditions of the call, including the compliance with the EU values (in case of partnership) (in .pdf format),

● A scanned valid statute or founding act of the applicant, if the document is not available in a publicly accessible national electronic registry (in .pdf format),

● A scanned valid founding act or statute of the partner, if the document is not available in a publicly accessible national electronic registry (in .pdf format).

Applicants will be notified on the result of their application no later than 14 days after their submission. All applications received shall be assessed according to the selection criteria published in the call. Applicants can submit new application any time after the rejection of the previous one. At the same time, an applicant can have only one on-going ”go out and vote” action.

Evaluation process (apply to both countries):

Administrative check of administrative and eligibility criteria (consortium staff, 4 eyes rule) (see the criteria in the Call document). If certain parts of the project application are missing and can be supplemented (documents or information), applicants will have 5 working days from the date of notification to submit the required supplements. The notification requesting the supplement will be sent to the email address provided by the applicant in the application form (the email address of the contact person).

Applicants whose applications are rejected due to non-compliance with administrative and eligibility criteria will have 8 working days from the date of notification to submit an appeal against the eligibility decision. Appeals will be reviewed by the Complaints Committee, and the Committee’s decision is final. Appeals should be sent to the designated email address for Slovenia/Croatia.

Evaluation of Application Quality (apply to both countries):

Each application that meets the administrative and eligibility criteria will be reviewed and assessed by collective decision-making of the evaluation commission, consisting of 5 members – 3 representatives of the consortium, 2 external experts (1 from Slovenia and 1 from Croatia). As the call will take place on a rolling basis according to a “first come – first serve” principle, there will be no scoring, only YES/NO decisions on each of the criteria (with argumentation). Only projects with all criteria assessed with YES will be supported (see the criteria in the Call document).

Rejected applications can be re-submitted any time, until all funds are exhausted or until 01/01/2028 at the latest.

Due diligence: all proposals that are confirmed by the evaluation committee will be checked on the respect of respect of EU values and double funding.

Activities that would promote specific political party or candidates are NOT eligible.

results.summary: AMU Scholarships for the internship of the Master 2 « Biology & Health », study-track « AI and biomarkers » within the European Project « Advanced Digital Skills AI and Health ».
results.content: AMU Scholarships for the internship of the Master 2 « Biology & Health », study-track « AI and biomarkers » within the European Project « Advanced Digital Skills AI and Health ».

beneficiaryAdministration:
Purpose : Aix-Marseille Université is opening applications for granting and paying funds for the traineeship period of students enrolled in Master 2 « Biology & Health », study-track « Biomarkers and AI » at the Faculty of Medical & Paramedical Sciences.

The hosting organism : The aim of the action is to provide the allocation required during the training period in work-placement by the French Law regarding traineeships lasting more than 2 months, which must be paid in the form of daily allowance for work-placement (4,35 €/ hours) for a actual working time not exceeding 10 hours per day. Legal working week cannot exceed 35 hours.

The principles and procedure for awarding funding is granted through a list of internships, which are proposed in line with the thematic area of the programme AI and Health and its implementation. Combination with another European funded grant, such as the allowance awarded as part of the mobility for traineeship within the Programme Erasmus+ is not allowed, due to the question of possible double-funding.

Participants must be EU citizens with a European nationality to be eligible for European funding under the project "Advanced Digital Skills AI and Health".

Applications :

The student interested by an internship must be enrolled in Master 2 « Biology & Health », study-track « AI and biomarkers » at Aix-Marseille Université to acquire academic qualifications corresponding to this level. Applicants must send the following documents :

  1. the completed form and attachments, which must be returned by e-mail to Mrs Nicole Haroun : nicole.haroun@univ-amu.fr , project manager for the European project « AI and Health ».

The attachments are a cover letter explaining the motivations to undertake an internship, a CV, the internship request form (the form of Aix-Marseille Université is available on the link : https://aiandhealth.eu/ ), proof of liability insurance, copy of the student card or certificate of enrolment at the university and ID card.

Selection criteria : the choice of the location of the traineeship is the prevailing factor in deciding who gets the scholarship, depending on the location of the internship on the French mainland and oversea territories or in a third country not associated to the Programme Erasmus+. The decision of awarding the allowance is made on the basis of internship requirements, merit and individual qualifications of the student.

Weight of evaluation criteria :

1.the thematic subject of the internship should be perfectly in line with the objective of the Master (3/5 points);

2.the great potential for publication in connection with the results achieved during the internship (1/5 points);

3.acquisition of new digital and technical skills (1/5 points).

The applications of successful candidates are selected by representatives of the pedagogical team of the Master « Biology & Health », which comprises at least 3 members of the pedagogical team, including one representative from the Institut Laënnec.
description:
The internship period must be in line with the objective of the Master :

- a complete understanding on how AI is used in biomedical and healthcare research,

- a better identification, a controlled development and validation of biomarkers used for prevention, diagnosis or monitoring diseases,

- a more appropriate use of Information Technology tools and methods to analyse the data to exploit the full potential of large datasets from medical and biological research,

- the latest AI operating techniques, such as machine learning and deep learning, to propose innovative solution in personalised medicine,

- designing, planing and conducting high-impact research,

- the participation in interdisciplinary research project involving skills in biology, AI and bio-informatics, by identifying specificlly required input from each main scientific area to come up with innovative solutions in the health field.

results.content: FuseNet Support of Master Students in attending Educational Events

beneficiaryAdministration:
The submission of applications is done via the FuseNet website. The submitted applications are evaluated by the FuseNet Executive Office. Decision to the student will be communicated by email, typically within 2 weeks after complete submission of the application.

Only in case of doubt regarding eligibility, the FuseNet Executive Office consults the Academic Council of FuseNet (in written procedure). The decision of the Academic Council of FuseNet is final and binding and cannot be discussed or changed again.
description:
This support scheme is launched to support and facilitate Master students to take part in educational activities external to their own organization. It allows Master students to participate in fusion Master classes, summer schools, and other short-term events with a dominant educational character. All conferences are excluded from support except when the Master student has his/her own contribution at the event (see terms and conditions for details).

Students registered at universities that are a FuseNet member and/or are seeking to attend educational activities at hosts that are a FuseNet member, and both the home university and the educational event are located in one of the countries that are part of the EUROfusion member states, can apply here for financial support to take part in a fusion-related educational training activity.

The financial support consists of a fixed amount of travel support (depending on the travel distance) and subsistence support (depending on the duration). The (training) activity has to take place at a university group or research institute in one of the EUROfusion members states or at a FuseNet member institute. The application has to be submitted at least 2 weeks before the actual start of the educational event. The educational event has to start no later than 6 months after application.
