results.content: UPC-AI4CI 1st Scholarship Call

beneficiaryAdministration:
1.Summary and purpose of the call

The Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya – Barcelona TECH (hereinafter “UPC”) is soliciting applications for scholarships grants (hereinafter “scholarships”) to support students of the master's degree program “Artificial Intelligence for Connected Industries” (hereinafter “AI4CI Master”) taught at UPC Castelldefels School of Telecommunications and Aerospace Engineering (hereinafter “EETAC”) in Castelldefels, Spain

The UPC- AI4CI scholarships is granted by the “Artificial Intelligence for Connected Industries” (hereinafter “AI4CI project”). The AI4CI project is co-funded by the European Union within the under the Grant Agreement No. 101123524 funded under the topic DIGITAL-2022-SKILLS-03-SPECIALISED-EDU - Specialised education programmes or modules in key capacity areas.

The maximum funding available under this call is €167,500 and may be awarded until the available budget is fully exhausted, provided that this occurs within the overall implementation period of the AI4CI project.

The indicative total number of scholarships to be awarded is approximately 49 ranging from 500 EUR to 4,500 EUR.

The aim of the scholarships is that recipients benefit from AI4CI project's high-quality education in digital areas and to promote equality and excellence in the field of computer science and AI, as well as to increase the accessibility of master's studies developing advanced digital skills and promote the growth of higher-level skills, equality and diversity in computer science.

Converging towards gender equality in ICT fields in EU and the socioeconomic status of the applicant are factors that will be taken into account in the selection process but everyone is welcome to apply regardless their gender and/or socioeconomic situation

This call covers the cohorts 2025-2027 and 2026-2028.

2. Characteristics of support

The scholarship will be awarded to persons (hereinafter referred to as applicants) who are citizens of the European Union, listed EEA countries or of countries associated to Digital Europe Programme and who are currently studying in the AI4CI project master's degree program “AI4CI Master” at “EETAC” in Castelldefels, Spain; as well as those students who have already been pre-admitted to the “AI4CI Master” (2026-2027) and are expected to complete their enrolment in the coming weeks and those who will be admitted to the “AI4CI Master” for the course 2027-2028.

This call offers 4 different support modalities, as described below. Applicants may apply for a combination of different support modalities. However, regardless of the combination of modalities requested, the maximum aggregate scholarship amount that may be awarded to any eligible student is 4.500€.

The maximum amount specified for each modality applies only to that specific modality. Therefore, while different modalities may be combined, the total scholarship amount awarded to any individual student shall not exceed 4.500€. Consequently, no student may receive the maximum amount available under all four modalities simultaneously.

2.1 Reimbursement of tuition fees

Reimbursement of tuition fees includes:                         

  1. The enrollment tuition costs for the full master's program which must be paid before the end of the project.
  2. Administrative and support fees.
  3. The cost of issuance of the official title (if paid before the end of the project)

Each EU beneficiary can be reimbursed up to a maximum of 3.400€. Supporting documentation for the costs incurred will be required.

2.2 Contribution to living and transportation expenses

The scholarship supports living and/or transportation expenses. In particular, it covers a monthly allowance of 100 € for a maximum of 6 months between the resolution of the concession and the end of the project.

Each beneficiary can receive a maximum of 600€. Supporting documentation for the costs incurred will be required towards reimbursement purposes.

2.3 Contribution to expenses for mobility stays related to the master program

The scholarship supports expenses for in person mobility stays not covered by the Erasmus+ Program related to the AI4CI master program. They must be incurred while the student is enrolled in the program and before the end of the project.

In particular, it supports living, transportation and accommodation expenses related to study collaboration visit to another institution, academic stay at another institution for the master thesis or attendance to courses taught at another university within the framework of the master program.

Each beneficiary can receive a maximum of 500€. Supporting documentation for the costs incurred will be required towards reimbursement purposes.

2.4 Other study-related expenses

The scholarship supports expenses for the purchase of hardware and/or software necessary to study; for the acquisition of additional training or information sources, improvement of the necessary competencies and for other study-related expenses. The maximum amount for this modality is up to 1.100€.

3.    Requirements for applicants

1.  Candidates must have been already admitted to the AI4CI master at UPC EETAC or applied to be admitted for the academic year. This means that to be considered for the scholarship, applicants must apply concurrently to the master's program for the cohort 2026-2028 or be already enrolled in the program from the cohort 2025-2027.

2.  Being a full-time degree-seeking student in the AI4CI master's degree program (corresponding to 30 ECTS per semester).

3.  To be an EU citizen or a citizen of one of the listed EEA countries or of one of the countries associated to Digital Europe Programme – provide a copy of the identity document indicating nationality;

4.  For modality 2.2, having monthly rental expenses of at least 200€ or living at a distance of UPC Castelldefels of at least 20 km.

5.For modality 2. 3, the expenses have to be related to the AI4CI master program.

6.  For modality 2.4 a justification letter together with the corresponding quotation(s) dated within the previous 15 days to the application and final related invoices and proof of payments.

4.    Applications

Applications may be submitted according to the following cut-off dates, provided that the maximum available budget has not been exhausted:

  1. 29th September 2026 (23:59h Brussels time).
  2. 5th February 2027 (23:59h Brussels time).
  3. 5th July 2027 (23:59h Brussels time).

The application must be submitted through the UPC Electronic Office filling in the UPC-AI4CI scholarships form. The link is as follows: https://seuelectronica.upc.edu/.

The following documentation has to be attached to the application form:

  1. Cover letter stating the following: presentation of the candidate detailing their academic merits, the motivation and plans, how the received scholarship will be used, how it will contribute to the student’s upskilling in advanced digital skills, and the description of their socioeconomic situation (personal, social, economic, work, etc.) that may be relevant to obtaining the scholarship (mandatory for all modalities);
  2. Documentary evidence of the situations described in the previous point (mandatory for all modalities);
  3. A copy of the identity document showing the date of birth and nationality of the applicant (mandatory for all modalities);
  4. For modality 2.2 also provide documentary evidence of meeting the rental or distance requirements established in point 3.4.
  5. For modality 2.3 also provide information about the mobility stay, letter explaining the purpose and relationship with the master program and budget.
  6. For modality 2.4 also provide information about the hardware or software purpose of study plus a quotation dated within the previous 15 days to the application and the corresponding invoices and proof of payments. The same will apply with regard to the acquisition of additional or information sources towards the improvement of the necessary competencies or other study-related expenses not covered by modalities 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3.

5.     Selection criteria

The selection committee (please refer to clause 7) will evaluate the applications taking into account the academic merit of the candidate as well as the gender and socioeconomic disparities in engineering and computer science.

For modality 2.3, the relationship of the expenses with the AI4CI master program will be checked.

In particular, per each modality, a formula of 8 points based on academic merit and 2 points for gender and socioeconomic situation (1 point if female and 1 point if last year annual income has been less than 21.000€ per year) for a total of 10 points will be assigned to each candidate based on the information candidates provide to the committee. Both the master's program application documents and the additional documentation provided for this scholarship application will be taken into account.

Applications that fulfill the eligibility criteria but are not awarded because of budget limitations will be included in a reserve list (one per each modality). In case one of the awarded candidates can’t accept or refuses the scholarship or loses the financial support, the first candidate in the corresponding reserve list will be automatically re-considered for assessment.

6.    Resolution

Applications for modalities 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3 will be continuously assessed.

Within 5 working days after the reception of applications, the selection committee assesses the received applications, their suitability, award points according to the criteria set out in clause 5 and thus rank the applicants. The selection committee selects the best-ranked applicants, but only those who fully meet the Scholarship requirements described in this call.

Scholarship resolutions related to this call will be published through UPC’s Electronic Notice Board (https://seuelectronica.upc.edu/ca/etauler/e-tauler), “e-Tauler”. and will be communicated to all candidates by the selection committee by e-mail on the same day the resolutions are published. All information about awarded scholarships will be published at the UPC-AI4CI Scholarship website.

7.    Payment conditions

Payments related to each modality will be done according to the following schedule, namely:

1. Awarded students coming from the cohort 2025-2027:

  1. 1st Instalment: 21st October 2026.
  2. 2nd Instalment: 29th February 2027.
  3. 2nd Instalment: 30th July 2027.

2. Awarded students coming from the cohort 2026-2028:

  1. 1st Instalment: 29th February 2027.
  2. 2nd Instalment: 30th July 2027. 

8.    Selection committee

The selection committee will be integrated by the members of the Master’s Committee of the AI4CI master program, which currently are:

  1. Prof. Cristina Cervelló-Pastor.
  2. Prof. David Rincón Rivera.
  3. Prof. Carles Gómez Montenegro.

9.    Obligations for applicants

Students who have received Scholarships, within 5 working days upon notification, must present to the selection committee the following documents:

a.      A signed scholarship award agreement, which also specifies the consent to the processing of the student's personal data, for scholarship management and marketing purposes and a series of legal obligations that apply to students receiving the support such as respect of ethics, record-keeping, etc.

b.      Provide the bank details necessary for the transfer of the scholarship.

c. Provide a written declaration, justifying the absence of EU double funding in forms of scholarships.

d.      Document demonstrating that the applicant has successfully completed a minimum of 22.5 ECTS per semester (~75 %).

10. Right of appeal

Students have the right to appeal about the results of the assessment, presenting aspects that they consider inappropriate in their assessment, factual errors in the assessment of the data provided. In the case of an appeal, the following procedure shall apply:

·Appeals are accepted by the study programme committee within 10 working days from the date of notification of the results of the assessment;

  1. The appeal must be submitted in writing, indicating the specific places where the student's score was improperly assessed;
  2. The study program committee must evaluate the appeal within 14 working days and inform the applicant about its results;
  3. If the inaccuracies indicated in the appeal are confirmed, they must be corrected and, accordingly, the order of award of the scholarship is updated.

In the event of a refusal of the scholarship, disagreement with the conditions or failure to provide the necessary data in a timely manner, the applicant is not included in the list of scholarship recipients, and for the occupation of this scholarship, the next priority applicant who is on the reserve list is contacted.

11.  Incompatibilities

This scholarship is incompatible with any other scholarship, grant, or financial support covering the same eligible expenses in order to avoid multiple funding for the same purposes.

12. Payment arrangements

Funds will be disbursed directly to the scholarship recipients upon verification that all eligibility conditions have been met. Recipients of scholarship financial support for all modalities will provide the eligible expenses actually incurred and presented (corresponding invoices and/or tickets and their corresponding proofs of payment) after the completion of each semester.


For modality 2.1, scholarships will cover the tuition fees of any semester’s courses until the end of the project as described above.


For modality 2.2, scholarships will cover the allocated monthly amount corresponding to the number of months in which the student is enrolled to the program between the awarding of the scholarship and the end of the project.


For modalities 2.3, scholarships will cover the actual expenses incurred up to the established maximum.


In case of non-continuation of the Master Program by the recipient no further support will be given. Supporting documentation for the incurred costs will be required. Costs will be eligible if declared eligible in the agreement and if they fulfill the general eligibility conditions established for the EU Funding Programmes 2021-2027.

13. Data protection

Applicant’s personal data will be processed by the EETAC of UPC, as data controller, will process your personal data in accordance with the provisions of General Data Protection Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 April 2016 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data, and repealing Directive 95/46/EC (GDPR), and Organic Law 3/2018 of 5 December on the protection of personal data and guarantee of digital rights.


The personal data processing activity being carried out is “F01.6 Management of scholarships and study grants”, for the purpose of managing this call, as well as any actions derived from it. The legal basis for processing is the performance of a task carried out in the public interest (Article 6.1.e of the GDPR) and compliance with legal obligations (Article 6.1.c of the GDPR).


In compliance with the principles of publicity and transparency, and in accordance with the aforementioned regulations and administrative procedure legislation, applicants are informed that the identifying data of candidate (both beneficiaries and those on the waiting list) may be published on the website of the call, on the UPC Transparent portal, and UPC’s Electronic Notice Board (e-Tauler), in accordance with the provisions of Section 6.


The personal data provided will be retained for the time necessary to fulfil the purpose for which they were collected, to determine any potential liabilities that may arise, and in accordance with archive and document regulations. Notwithstanding the foregoing, personal data may be stored for longer periods insofar as the personal data will be processed solely for archiving purposes in the public interest, scientific or historical research purposes, or statistical purposes, subject to the implementation of the appropriate technical and organizational measures to safeguard the rights and freedoms of individuals.


Data subjects may exercise their rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, data portability, or objection to the processing of their data, under the terms provided by current legislation, through the Electronic Office (https://seuelectronica.upc.edu/ca/tots-els-tramits/Exercici_drets_relatius_proteccio_dades_personals) or by writing to the data controller at the postal address c/Jordi Girona, 31 – 08034 Barcelona. title: Specialised education programmes or modules in key capacity areas
destinationDetails:
1.Summary and purpose of the call

The Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya – Barcelona TECH (hereinafter “UPC”) is soliciting applications for scholarships grants (hereinafter “scholarships”) to support students of the master's degree program “Artificial Intelligence for Connected Industries” (hereinafter “AI4CI Master”) taught at UPC Castelldefels School of Telecommunications and Aerospace Engineering (hereinafter “EETAC”) in Castelldefels, Spain

The UPC- AI4CI scholarships is granted by the “Artificial Intelligence for Connected Industries” (hereinafter “AI4CI project”). The AI4CI project is co-funded by the European Union within the under the Grant Agreement No. 101123524 funded under the topic DIGITAL-2022-SKILLS-03-SPECIALISED-EDU - Specialised education programmes or modules in key capacity areas.

The maximum funding available under this call is €167,500 and may be awarded until the available budget is fully exhausted, provided that this occurs within the overall implementation period of the AI4CI project.

The indicative total number of scholarships to be awarded is approximately 49 ranging from 500 EUR to 4,500 EUR.

The aim of the scholarships is that recipients benefit from AI4CI project's high-quality education in digital areas and to promote equality and excellence in the field of computer science and AI, as well as to increase the accessibility of master's studies developing advanced digital skills and promote the growth of higher-level skills, equality and diversity in computer science.

Converging towards gender equality in ICT fields in EU and the socioeconomic status of the applicant are factors that will be taken into account in the selection process but everyone is welcome to apply regardless their gender and/or socioeconomic situation

This call covers the cohorts 2025-2027 and 2026-2028.

2. Characteristics of support

The scholarship will be awarded to persons (hereinafter referred to as applicants) who are citizens of the European Union, listed EEA countries or of countries associated to Digital Europe Programme and who are currently studying in the AI4CI project master's degree program “AI4CI Master” at “EETAC” in Castelldefels, Spain; as well as those students who have already been pre-admitted to the “AI4CI Master” (2026-2027) and are expected to complete their enrolment in the coming weeks and those who will be admitted to the “AI4CI Master” for the course 2027-2028.

This call offers 4 different support modalities, as described below. Applicants may apply for a combination of different support modalities. However, regardless of the combination of modalities requested, the maximum aggregate scholarship amount that may be awarded to any eligible student is 4.500€.

The maximum amount specified for each modality applies only to that specific modality. Therefore, while different modalities may be combined, the total scholarship amount awarded to any individual student shall not exceed 4.500€. Consequently, no student may receive the maximum amount available under all four modalities simultaneously.

2.1 Reimbursement of tuition fees

Reimbursement of tuition fees includes:                         

  1. The enrollment tuition costs for the full master's program which must be paid before the end of the project.
  2. Administrative and support fees.
  3. The cost of issuance of the official title (if paid before the end of the project)

Each EU beneficiary can be reimbursed up to a maximum of 3.400€. Supporting documentation for the costs incurred will be required.

2.2 Contribution to living and transportation expenses

The scholarship supports living and/or transportation expenses. In particular, it covers a monthly allowance of 100 € for a maximum of 6 months between the resolution of the concession and the end of the project.

Each beneficiary can receive a maximum of 600€. Supporting documentation for the costs incurred will be required towards reimbursement purposes.

2.3 Contribution to expenses for mobility stays related to the master program

The scholarship supports expenses for in person mobility stays not covered by the Erasmus+ Program related to the AI4CI master program. They must be incurred while the student is enrolled in the program and before the end of the project.

In particular, it supports living, transportation and accommodation expenses related to study collaboration visit to another institution, academic stay at another institution for the master thesis or attendance to courses taught at another university within the framework of the master program.

Each beneficiary can receive a maximum of 500€. Supporting documentation for the costs incurred will be required towards reimbursement purposes.

2.4 Other study-related expenses

The scholarship supports expenses for the purchase of hardware and/or software necessary to study; for the acquisition of additional training or information sources, improvement of the necessary competencies and for other study-related expenses. The maximum amount for this modality is up to 1.100€.

3.    Requirements for applicants

1.  Candidates must have been already admitted to the AI4CI master at UPC EETAC or applied to be admitted for the academic year. This means that to be considered for the scholarship, applicants must apply concurrently to the master's program for the cohort 2026-2028 or be already enrolled in the program from the cohort 2025-2027.

2.  Being a full-time degree-seeking student in the AI4CI master's degree program (corresponding to 30 ECTS per semester).

3.  To be an EU citizen or a citizen of one of the listed EEA countries or of one of the countries associated to Digital Europe Programme – provide a copy of the identity document indicating nationality;

4.  For modality 2.2, having monthly rental expenses of at least 200€ or living at a distance of UPC Castelldefels of at least 20 km.

5.For modality 2. 3, the expenses have to be related to the AI4CI master program.

6.  For modality 2.4 a justification letter together with the corresponding quotation(s) dated within the previous 15 days to the application and final related invoices and proof of payments.

4.    Applications

Applications may be submitted according to the following cut-off dates, provided that the maximum available budget has not been exhausted:

  1. 29th September 2026 (23:59h Brussels time).
  2. 5th February 2027 (23:59h Brussels time).
  3. 5th July 2027 (23:59h Brussels time).

The application must be submitted through the UPC Electronic Office filling in the UPC-AI4CI scholarships form. The link is as follows: https://seuelectronica.upc.edu/.

The following documentation has to be attached to the application form:

  1. Cover letter stating the following: presentation of the candidate detailing their academic merits, the motivation and plans, how the received scholarship will be used, how it will contribute to the student’s upskilling in advanced digital skills, and the description of their socioeconomic situation (personal, social, economic, work, etc.) that may be relevant to obtaining the scholarship (mandatory for all modalities);
  2. Documentary evidence of the situations described in the previous point (mandatory for all modalities);
  3. A copy of the identity document showing the date of birth and nationality of the applicant (mandatory for all modalities);
  4. For modality 2.2 also provide documentary evidence of meeting the rental or distance requirements established in point 3.4.
  5. For modality 2.3 also provide information about the mobility stay, letter explaining the purpose and relationship with the master program and budget.
  6. For modality 2.4 also provide information about the hardware or software purpose of study plus a quotation dated within the previous 15 days to the application and the corresponding invoices and proof of payments. The same will apply with regard to the acquisition of additional or information sources towards the improvement of the necessary competencies or other study-related expenses not covered by modalities 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3.

5.     Selection criteria

The selection committee (please refer to clause 7) will evaluate the applications taking into account the academic merit of the candidate as well as the gender and socioeconomic disparities in engineering and computer science.

For modality 2.3, the relationship of the expenses with the AI4CI master program will be checked.

In particular, per each modality, a formula of 8 points based on academic merit and 2 points for gender and socioeconomic situation (1 point if female and 1 point if last year annual income has been less than 21.000€ per year) for a total of 10 points will be assigned to each candidate based on the information candidates provide to the committee. Both the master's program application documents and the additional documentation provided for this scholarship application will be taken into account.

Applications that fulfill the eligibility criteria but are not awarded because of budget limitations will be included in a reserve list (one per each modality). In case one of the awarded candidates can’t accept or refuses the scholarship or loses the financial support, the first candidate in the corresponding reserve list will be automatically re-considered for assessment.

6.    Resolution

Applications for modalities 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3 will be continuously assessed.

Within 5 working days after the reception of applications, the selection committee assesses the received applications, their suitability, award points according to the criteria set out in clause 5 and thus rank the applicants. The selection committee selects the best-ranked applicants, but only those who fully meet the Scholarship requirements described in this call.

Scholarship resolutions related to this call will be published through UPC’s Electronic Notice Board (https://seuelectronica.upc.edu/ca/etauler/e-tauler), “e-Tauler”. and will be communicated to all candidates by the selection committee by e-mail on the same day the resolutions are published. All information about awarded scholarships will be published at the UPC-AI4CI Scholarship website.

7.    Payment conditions

Payments related to each modality will be done according to the following schedule, namely:

1. Awarded students coming from the cohort 2025-2027:

  1. 1st Instalment: 21st October 2026.
  2. 2nd Instalment: 29th February 2027.
  3. 2nd Instalment: 30th July 2027.

2. Awarded students coming from the cohort 2026-2028:

  1. 1st Instalment: 29th February 2027.
  2. 2nd Instalment: 30th July 2027. 

8.    Selection committee

The selection committee will be integrated by the members of the Master’s Committee of the AI4CI master program, which currently are:

  1. Prof. Cristina Cervelló-Pastor.
  2. Prof. David Rincón Rivera.
  3. Prof. Carles Gómez Montenegro.

9.    Obligations for applicants

Students who have received Scholarships, within 5 working days upon notification, must present to the selection committee the following documents:

a.      A signed scholarship award agreement, which also specifies the consent to the processing of the student's personal data, for scholarship management and marketing purposes and a series of legal obligations that apply to students receiving the support such as respect of ethics, record-keeping, etc.

b.      Provide the bank details necessary for the transfer of the scholarship.

c. Provide a written declaration, justifying the absence of EU double funding in forms of scholarships.

d.      Document demonstrating that the applicant has successfully completed a minimum of 22.5 ECTS per semester (~75 %).

10. Right of appeal

Students have the right to appeal about the results of the assessment, presenting aspects that they consider inappropriate in their assessment, factual errors in the assessment of the data provided. In the case of an appeal, the following procedure shall apply:

·Appeals are accepted by the study programme committee within 10 working days from the date of notification of the results of the assessment;

  1. The appeal must be submitted in writing, indicating the specific places where the student's score was improperly assessed;
  2. The study program committee must evaluate the appeal within 14 working days and inform the applicant about its results;
  3. If the inaccuracies indicated in the appeal are confirmed, they must be corrected and, accordingly, the order of award of the scholarship is updated.

In the event of a refusal of the scholarship, disagreement with the conditions or failure to provide the necessary data in a timely manner, the applicant is not included in the list of scholarship recipients, and for the occupation of this scholarship, the next priority applicant who is on the reserve list is contacted.

11.  Incompatibilities

This scholarship is incompatible with any other scholarship, grant, or financial support covering the same eligible expenses in order to avoid multiple funding for the same purposes.

12. Payment arrangements

Funds will be disbursed directly to the scholarship recipients upon verification that all eligibility conditions have been met. Recipients of scholarship financial support for all modalities will provide the eligible expenses actually incurred and presented (corresponding invoices and/or tickets and their corresponding proofs of payment) after the completion of each semester.


For modality 2.1, scholarships will cover the tuition fees of any semester’s courses until the end of the project as described above.


For modality 2.2, scholarships will cover the allocated monthly amount corresponding to the number of months in which the student is enrolled to the program between the awarding of the scholarship and the end of the project.


For modalities 2.3, scholarships will cover the actual expenses incurred up to the established maximum.


In case of non-continuation of the Master Program by the recipient no further support will be given. Supporting documentation for the incurred costs will be required. Costs will be eligible if declared eligible in the agreement and if they fulfill the general eligibility conditions established for the EU Funding Programmes 2021-2027.

The Joint Call follows a two-stage application and evaluation procedure.


Pre-proposals must be submitted electronically through the FOREST Electronic Submission and Evaluation System (ESES). They will undergo a formal eligibility check by the Call Office, national/regional eligibility checks by the relevant Research Funding Organisations, and scientific evaluation by an independent International Expert Panel.


Following the first-stage evaluation, selected consortia will be invited to submit full proposals. Full proposals will undergo a further formal and national/regional eligibility check and independent scientific evaluation by the International Expert Panel.


Final recommendations for funding will be made by the Call Steering Committee on the basis of the scientific evaluation, ranking lists and available national/regional and EU funding.

description:
The FOREST Joint Call 2026 – ForestPathways supports transnational research and innovation activities across the spectrum from fundamental research to applied research and, where appropriate, demonstration activities. Projects are expected to generate new knowledge, develop practical solutions, and contribute to implementation in policy, management or industry contexts, while considering the diversity of forests and the forest-based sector.

Applicants must select the single topic that best reflects the primary focus of their proposal. Proposals may address multiple topics but will be evaluated and ranked under one primary topic.

TOPIC 1 – Climate-Resilient Forest Systems: “How forests function and respond to climate change”

This topic supports research and innovation addressing the resilience, adaptive capacity, and long-term sustainability of forest ecosystems under changing environmental conditions, including climate change and increasing disturbance pressures. It aims to strengthen the scientific basis for climate-resilient forest systems and support their adaptation and mitigation to climate change, within broader environmental and socioeconomic contexts.

Proposals should address, where relevant, carbon dynamics measurement, monitoring and assessment of carbon stocks and sinks; adaptation pathways and strategies; forest ecosystem processes and dynamics; disturbance regimes, including wildfires and other abiotic and biotic disturbances, pests and diseases; landscape-level interactions and spatial dynamics; and genetic diversity and adaptive capacity, including assisted migration.

TOPIC 2 – Adaptive and Multifunctional Forest Management Systems: “How forests should be managed under changing conditions”

This topic supports research and innovation focused on the implementation of adaptive and multifunctional forest management systems that enhance resilience, sustainability, and the provision of multiple ecosystem services. It aims to support forest management approaches capable of responding to ecological change, disturbance risks, and evolving environmental, economic, and societal demands.

Proposals should address, where relevant, silvicultural systems and management approaches supporting resilient and multifunctional forests; sustainable harvesting and wood mobilisation methods; monitoring, assessment and planning tools for adaptive management; integration of forest genetic resources into management strategies; operational, digital and technical innovations; risk reduction and adaptation strategies; and trade-offs and synergies between ecosystem services.

TOPIC 3 – Timber and Innovative Wood-Based Products: “How wood is transformed into innovative products”

This topic supports research and innovation on the development, performance, and uptake of timber and innovative wood-based products contributing to decarbonisation and the circular bioeconomy. It aims to advance the development and market uptake of sustainable wood-based products and systems, supporting the substitution of fossil-based and carbon-intensive materials and contributing to low-carbon construction and manufacturing.

Proposals should address, where relevant, engineered timber and timber construction systems; high-value wood-based products, chemicals and materials; substitution of fossil-based and other carbon-intensive materials; more sustainable alternatives to polluting wood treatments and processing practices; standardisation, testing and certification; circular and resource-efficient use of wood-based products; innovative use of underutilised softwood and hardwood species; innovative manufacturing technologies; and approaches to increase market demand and consumer acceptance and uptake.

TOPIC 4 – Forest Value Chains, Markets and Governance: “How forest-based sectors, markets and governance are organised”

This topic supports research and innovation strengthening the resilience, sustainability, and functioning of forest-based value chains, markets, and governance systems, supporting the transition towards a sustainable and circular forest-based bioeconomy. It aims to support resilient, sustainable, competitive, and innovative forest-based value chains and governance systems capable of responding to environmental, economic, and societal transitions.

Proposals should address, where relevant, forest-based value chains and market organisation; innovative business models, economic viability and investment readiness; policy, regulatory and governance instruments; barriers to market uptake and innovation deployment; cascading use, circularity and efficient resource use; skills, labour, education and workforce development; and European resilience in sustainable raw material supply, value chains, local processing capacities and forest-based economies.

The topics provide strategic direction and facilitate evaluation. They are not exhaustive and do not restrict the submission of innovative or cross-cutting proposals aligned with the overall objectives of the call.

description:
The aim of the call is to support the creation, development and practical validation of scalable solutions that address the documented needs of the Czech cybersecurity ecosystem. Supported projects must combine design or development, at least one pilot deployment or practical validation, evaluation of results and preparation for further use. The call is focused on three thematic areas:

The call is focused on three main thematic pillars:

• Scalable solutions for the resilience of small and medium-sized enterprises: new or significantly expanded services and tools to protect small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), self-assessment, prioritisation of measures and sector- specific implementation packages.

• Implementation tools and services for compliance readiness, management and risk management: practical solutions for NIS2, CRA, DORA, supply chain security, cybersecurity management, record-keeping, reporting, secure development, SBOM and vulnerability management.

• Services and technical solutions for incident preparedness, response and recovery: standardised services, sector-specific scenarios, exercise packages and tools for recovery testing, record-keeping, escalation and reporting.

Support will be given primarily to projects that aim to deliver solutions with a measurable impact on a wider target group. Analyses alone, general training or documentation without implementation and validation activities are not a priority. Implementation by individual organisations is eligible primarily as a means of piloting the transferability and wider applicability of the results.

In accordance with the programme’s terms and conditions, the maximum amount of financial support is €100,000 and the minimum amount is €60,000 (in the form of a grant),depending on the current exchange rate of the Czech koruna. Projects will be funded at a rate of 50% of eligible costs, which means that the beneficiary will receive funding amounting to one half of the eligible costs incurred during the implementation of the project and substantiated in accordance with the established rules. The funding awarded to a project may be lower than the amount that was requested in the application. The decision on the final amount of support granted will depend on the quality of the project application, the consistency of the expected results with the proposed budget, and the structure of the individual planned costs.

Beneficiaries will be required to regularly provide evidence of actual expenditure incurred in connection with the implementation of the project. Details regarding the frequency and format of reporting will be specified in the grant agreement. Applicants must ensure that the project proposal meets the conditions designed to prevent the project funding from resulting in unauthorised indirect state aid within the meaning of relevant European legislation, or from leading to double funding.

The following types of organisations are eligible to participate in this call and meet the criteria set out in the EU Digital Europe programme:

• Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).

• Non-governmental organisations (NGOs) that demonstrate professional competence and the ability to produce and practically validate an output in line with the objectives of the call.

• Academic and research institutions are eligible only as members of a consortium that includes at least one small or medium-sized enterprise. They may not submit an application on their own.

Consortia may combine the above-mentioned entities. The application must specify the actual roles, responsibilities and budgets of the members; a formal partnership without evidence of added value is not sufficient.

beneficiaryAdministration:
More detailed information about the call may be found here

To apply, please complete the submission form on EU SURVEY

Applications may be modified as long as the deadline is respected: you will be able to save and come back later on EU Survey. The platform will be automatically closed at the date and time announced, that is November 30th, 2026, at 5:00 pm CET. Applicants will receive an e-mail confirming that their application has been well uploaded on the platform. Shall you not receive the confirmation e-mail, please contact Benjamin Schmidt at bes@energycluster.dk and copy your local contact point. SMEs applying as a consortium should fill in one proposal. One of the involved SMEs will act as a “coordinator” and will be responsible for the submission of the application.

RENEW BOOSTER Eurocluster innovation mechanism will support projects in the "challenges" call and projects in the "open" call, at least 3 SMEs and up to €60,000 euros per SME.


Evaluation Process and Criteria

All eligible applications will be evaluated by evaluators against the criteria defined in the RENEW-BOOSTER Call Text: Excellence, Impact and Quality and efficiency of implementation. Each criterion is scored from 0 to 10, with a minimum threshold of 6/10 per criterion.

Indicative timeline:

  1. Call deadline: 30 November 2026 (17:00 CET)
  2. Evaluation: December 2026
  3. Results communication: Mid-January 2027
  4. Contract signature: End-January 2027

For full details on the evaluation methodology, scoring, thresholds, and tie-breaking rules, please see the call text


Proposals will be eligible only if all the following conditions are met:

  1. Applicants must be established in one of the following eligible countries: EU-27 + countries participating in the SMP/COSME strand.
  2. Applicants must be SMEs according to the European Union definition of SMEs: the formal definition is available here and the SME self-assessment questionnaire is available here.
  3. Applications must address either the Challenge Call or the Open Call, as described in the Call Text. For applications submitted under the Challenge Call, detailed descriptions of the challenges can be found here or in the EUSurvey submission form.
  4. Applications must be written in English (applications partially written in another language are not eligible) and must not exceed the maximum number of characters stated in each text box of the pre-defined template available on the submission platform;
  5. Applications must be submitted through EU Survey
  6. SMEs may apply individually to the Challenge Call (Strand A). For the Open Call (Strand B), SMEs may apply either individually or as part of a consortium of up to 3 SMEs.
  7. Each SME may submit a maximum of one application under Strand A and one application under Strand B, whether applying individually or as part of a consortium. Applications submitted under both strands must address different activities and must not result in double funding. Any SME submitting more than one application to the same strand will be automatically disqualified.
  8. No annexes can be submitted other than the ones demanded on the EU Survey platform.
  9. Every applicant organisation needs to be registered on the EU F&T Portal and have a 9-digit Participant Identification Code (PIC). Please find all information PIC number.
  10. This call requires private co-funding. Further information can be found here on page 5-7.
  11. At least 10% of funded SMEs should come from countries or regions other than those represented in the consortium; Denmark, Norway, Poland, France, Bulgaria and Spain.
description:
The two calls will be structured through two distinct funding strands. It is reminded that the cumulative maximum FSTP support per SME under the whole set of RENEW-BOOSTER calls is EUR 60,000. An SME may submit a maximum of one application per strand, whether applying individually or as part of a consortium. Consequently, an SME may submit one application under Strand A and one application under Strand B, provided that the proposed activities are distinct and no double funding occurs.

Strand A (Challenge-driven) follows a two-step process linked to predefined industrial challenges. In Step 1, up to three SMEs per challenge receive €10,000 (with minimum 20% private co-funding) to develop and validate a proof of concept (TRL 6-7). After evaluation and a final pitch, one SME per challenge advances to Step 2 and receives €50,000 (with minimum 40% co-funding) to further develop and scale the solution (TRL 8–9).

Strand B (Open Call) follows a single-stage selection process. SMEs apply bottom-up and can request up to €10,000, €30,000, or €60,000 depending on project maturity, with increasing private co-funding requirements. Projects run up to six months.

Find more here: call text

callTitle: RENEW-BOOSTER EUROCLUSTER CALL N°2 FOR FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO THIRD PARTIES
furtherInformation:
The RENEW-BOOSTER project aims at driving innovation and industrialization in three critical sectors that are vital for Europe’s green transition and energy security: Photovoltaics (PV), Offshore Wind Energy, and the associated Energy Networks. At the core of RENEW-BOOSTER is the Accelerator, providing tailored support for SMEs to identify opportunities and develop solutions, strengthening their role in the renewable energy value chain and enhancing resilience.

The project aligns with Europe’s strategic priorities, including reducing critical raw material dependency (Critical Raw Materials Act), advancing climate goals (Green Deal), and supporting re-industrialization (Net Zero Industry Act). RENEW-BOOSTER aims to empower SMEs and accelerate Europe’s twin green and digital transitions.

We reserve the right not to award all available funds or to redistribute them between the different calls, depending on the proposals received and the results of the evaluation.

For answers to frequently asked questions, please visit our FAQ.

results.summary: NOSTRADAMUS - Open Call #1: Funding Digital Applications for Sustainable and Efficient Agriculture
results.content: NOSTRADAMUS - Open Call #1: Funding Digital Applications for Sustainable and Efficient Agriculture

beneficiaryAdministration:
Applications must be submitted electronically via the F6S platform: https://www.f6s.com/nostradamus-open-call-1/apply by 02 December 2026 at 17:00 CET.

All Open Call #1 documents are available for download at: https://nostradamus-project.eu/open-call-1/

Evaluation Workflow:

  1. Admissibility & Eligibility Check: Verification of submission criteria, official templates, language (English), single submission rules, country eligibility (EU Member States & Horizon Europe Associated Countries), and applicant eligibility (individual SMEs/start-ups/small mid-caps or 2-partner consortia).
  2. External Remote Expert Evaluation: Each eligible proposal is reviewed independently by two external experts against 4 criteria: Alignment (score 0–5), Excellence (score 0–5), Impact (score 0–5), and Implementation (score 0–5). Thresholds: min. 3/5 per criterion, min. 12/20 overall.  
  3. Consensus & Ranking: Expert review panel establishes a consensus report and topic ranking lists (one list per topic, 5 in total).  
  4. Online Interviews: The top 3 ranked proposals per topic undergo a 30-minute pitch and Q&A session with an Interview committee to finalize scores and ranking.  
  5. Final Selection & Contracting: Selection of 5 sub-projects (guaranteeing min. 1 project per topic T1–T5) followed by formal KYC verification and Sub-Grant Agreement signature.
description:
NOSTRADAMUS Open Call #1 invites system actors and innovators (SMEs, start-ups, small mid-caps, RTOs, end-user organisations) to design, develop, test, and validate multi-functional, open-source digital applications for farm decision-making and agribusiness.

Selected Third Parties will build upon the NOSTRADAMUS data infrastructure - including multi-dimensional Open Data Cubes, Analysis Ready Data (ARD) Earth Observation pipelines, real-time IoT Observatory streams, and socio-economic datasets - to deliver data-driven tools that optimize agricultural inputs (water, fertilizers, pesticides), improve energy balance, and enhance production resilience in cereal-based agricultural systems.

The call covers 5 designated topics:

  1. Topic 1 (T1): Sustainable crop production and optimisation of cereal-based systems under changing climate and soil conditions.
  2. Topic 2 (T2): Nutrient and soil health management, integrating soil fertility indicators, organic matter dynamics, and precision fertilisation models.  
  3. Topic 3 (T3): Water resource efficiency and drought resilience, using Early Warning System outputs and IoT-based soil moisture monitoring.  
  4. Topic 4 (T4): Smart and predictive pest and disease management to support the EU objective of reducing pesticide dependency.  
  5. Topic 5 (T5): Open topic (integrated, cross-domain decision-support applications combining at least two topics T1–T4).  

Awarded Third Parties must participate in a 12-month 4-Sprint program (Training, Design, Development & Validation, Demonstration & Assessment), physically demonstrate their application at 1 primary NOSTRADAMUS pilot site (DE, RS, CH, SI, or CY), deliver at least 1 user training session, release their source code as open-source, and author an EIP-AGRI Practice Abstract.

beneficiaryAdministration:
Article 2

Eligibility Criteria


Students enrolled in DIGISOC are eligible to apply for a scholarship only if they meet all of the following criteria:


1.  DIGISOC Students with EU Citizenship or Citizenship from one of the DEP Associates Countries

2.  Students who are enrolled in the second year of the DIGISOC programme for academic year 2026/2027.

3.  DIGISOC Students who have received at least 60 credits for DIGISOC programme courses and completed all courses in which they were enrolled.



Article 3

Application process and period for the academic year 2026/2027


The deadline to submit the applications for the DIGISOC scholarship is 14th December 2026 at 23.59 pm (CET – Central Europe Time).

Applicants are required to upload the necessary documents as listed below on the DIGISOC OpenOlat platform at the following link: 


https://lms.uibk.ac.at/auth/RepositoryEntry/5831590270/CourseNode/113899331829124


Applicants are required to upload the following materials in a single folder labeled with the applicant name:

1)    The signed Application Letter (Annex 1);

2)    The matriculation number at the University which is issuing this call;

3)    The supporting documentation for all eligibility criteria.

The application must be in English. Supporting documents may be submitted in English, Italian, German, or Czech; all other languages require certified translations. If the documentation is not sufficient, the Evaluation Committee mayrequest additional information or reject the application.


Article 4

Evaluation Committee

A joint Evaluation Committee, appointed by the Dean of the Faculty of Law of the Palacký University, reviews all applications and consists of:

·       One representative from each of the three DIGISOC degree awarding universities;

·       At least one DIGISOC student representative;

The Committee is appointed after the deadline for the application submission and terminates the evaluation process no later than 15 days after the deadline.


Article 5

Awarding Criteria and Evaluation Procedure


The joint Evaluation Committee will check eligibility criteria and evaluate each application.

The candidate academic excellence will be evaluated based on the weighted average of grades achieved during academic year 2025/2026 in all DIGISOC courses, calculated and rounded to hundredths (e.g. 28,77) on a 30 points scale according to the DIGISOC grade conversion table. Based on averages, students who have submitted their application will be put in descending order. In case of tie, they will be put on shared place, awarding the higher award.


To determine the exact amount of the scholarship allocated to each applicant, the joint Evaluation Committee will use the following model:


·      the Student with highest average will be awarded a 2000 EUR scholarship.

·      the Student with second highest average will be awarded a 1750 EUR scholarship.

·      the Student with third highest average will receive a 1500 EUR scholarship.

·      All other students with average above 26,99 will receive a scholarship which corresponds to the result of dividing the call's remaining budget by the number of applications fulfilling the award criteria, but not exceeding 1000 EUR per applicant.


The joint Evaluation Committee’s judgement is unquestionable.

The rankings and the exact amount of funding received by each applicant will be published on the DIGISOC website (https://digitalsociety4innovation.eu/costs-and-scholarships/) and the DIGISOC Awarding Universities Websites. This publication has the value of notification.
description:
Article 1

Purpose, amount and duration of the DIGISOC Scholarship


The Palacký University is issuing a Call for Application within the DIGISOC Scholarship Programme, reserved for students enrolled for the Academic Year 2026/2027 in the second year of the Joint Master’s Programme in Digital Society, Social Innovation and Global Citizenship (DIGISOC).

The Call for Application has a total budget of EUR 11.000,00.

The DIGISOC Scolarship Programme is designed to provide financial support to students participating in the DIGISOC Joint Master’s Programme (JMP) and aims to:

·      Reward students with outstanding academic performance;

·      Promote excellence in higher education;

·      Alleviate costs associated with tuition fees, summer schools, short-term mobilities, and living expenses.

The scholarships also function as a form of social support, helping students overcome personal or socio-economic obstacles that hinder participation in international education.

The DIGISOC scholarship is limited to one academic year. The scholarships are paid out in one instalment.

There is no automatic entitlement to scholarships and there is no automatic renewal.

The amount of the scholarship can reach a maximum of EUR 2.000,00 each (gross percipient) per academic year and applicant.

The exact amount of the Scholarship assigned to each applicant is based on the grade average based on criteria set in Article 5 – Award Criteria.

furtherInformation:
Article 6 Acceptance and Appeals


Applicants are notified of decisions within 15 days after the end of the submission period via e-mail. Rejected applications include a short justification.

Applicants who are not admitted to the scholarship have the right to appeal.

Appeals may be submitted by e-mail to programme coordinator and will be reviewed by the joint Evaluation Committee.

Within the mandatory deadline of 5 days from the date of receipt of the notice of the award of the scholarship, the applicant must send by e-mail to programme coordinator the declaration of acceptance (see Article 10) without reservation and under the conditions of the notice of competition, under penalty of forfeiture.

With said declaration, the scholarship assignee must also give explicit assurance to communicate any variation, which may occur during the year with respect to what has been declared.


Article 7

What to do to receive the scholarship


In order to administer the awarding of the scholarship, the scholarships assignee must provide Palacký University, Faculty of Law with the following documentation:

·      Enrollment certificate (complete with enrollment number);

·      Tax code;

·      Bank details (IBAN number, swift code, etc.);

·      Copy of passport.


Article 8

Eligibility Criteria

Students enrolled in DIGISOC for the second year are eligible to apply for a scholarship if they meet one or more of the following criteria:

1. Students with certified disabilities

Students with certified disabilities can apply for a DIGISOC scholarship. In the context of this call, and following Article 1 of the European Disability Policy, students with disabilities are considered students who have long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairments which, in interaction with various barriers, may hinder their full and effective participation in society on an equal basis with others. Applicants must provide certified medical documentation or proof of a national disability status.

2. Migrants or refugees

Students who are migrants or refugees can apply for funding based on their status. Required proof may include an asylum decision, a residence permit, or confirmation issued by a migration authority.

3. Students with low socio-economic family conditions

Students from families with low socio-economic conditions can apply for funding. Low socio-economic conditions are defined according to the student’s family income. Required proof may include a tax statement, an income certificate, or an official social benefit statement.

4. Students living in remote areas

Students living in a region in the lowest 25% of national population density and/or with no regular access to higher education within a 100 km radius may apply. Required proof is a residence certificate, which will be assessed against infrastructure data based on national statistics.


Application process and period for the academic year 2026/2027

The deadline to submit applications for the DIGISOC scholarships is 10. December 2026 at 23.59 CET (Central European Time).

Applicants are required to upload the necessary documents listed below on the DIGISOC OpenOlat platform at the following link:

https://lms.uibk.ac.at/auth/RepositoryEntry/5831590270/CourseNode/114518610654144

Applicants are required to upload the following materials in a single folder labelled with the applicant’s name:

·       The signed Application Letter (Annex 1);

·       The applicant’s registration number (Matrikelnummer) at the University of Innsbruck;

·       The supporting documentation for each claimed eligibility criterion, issued by a responsible authority or accredited expert.

·       The Data Protection and Consent Declaration (Annex 2).

The application must be in English. Supporting documents may be submitted in English, Italian, German, or Czech; documents in other languages require certified translations. If the documentation is insufficient, the Evaluation Committee may request additional information or reject the application.

By submitting the application and signing Annex 1, the applicant expressly confirms that the application has been submitted completely and correctly and that all information and supporting documents are accurate and complete. Incomplete applications may be excluded from the selection procedure.


Evaluation Committee

A joint Evaluation Committee, appointed by the Study Coordinator (Studienbeauftragter) of the Faculty of Economics and Statistics of the University of Innsbruck, reviews all applications and consists of:

·       One representative from each of the three DIGISOC degree-awarding universities;

·       At least one student representative from the University of Innsbruck;

·       Disability officer at the University of Innsbruck.

The Committee is appointed after the deadline for application submission and completes the evaluation process no later than 15 days after the deadline.


Awarding Criteria and Evaluation Procedure

The joint Evaluation Committee will evaluate each application and award points based on the following criteria:

1. Students with certified disabilities

Applicants will be awarded points on the basis of the severity and impact of their condition, ranging from 5 points for a comparatively less impactful disability to 10 points for a very serious disability.

2. Migrants or refugees

Applicants will be awarded points as follows: 

a.         10 points for refugee status; 

b.         10 points for migrant status with less than 5 years in the current country of residence; 

c.         5 points for migrant status with 5 or more years in the current country of residence.

3. Low socio-economic family condition

Applicants will be awarded 10 points if their family income falls within the first quartile (Q1), i.e. within the 25% of the population with the lowest incomes in their country of origin. Applicants will be awarded 5 points if their family income falls between the first and second quartile (Q2), i.e. within the range defined by the median income and Q1 in their country of origin. The reference fiscal year is the year preceding the year in which the application is submitted.

4. Remote areas

Applicants will be awarded 5 points for residence in a remote area. An additional 5 points will be awarded if the student’s residence is in a remote area with no regular access to higher education within a 100 km radius.

All applications will be ranked on the basis of the sum of points obtained across the four criteria. Each application can obtain a maximum of 30 points.

To determine the exact amount of the scholarship allocated to each applicant, the joint Evaluation Committee will use a proportional point-based model:

·       Total funds available are divided by the sum of all points awarded across valid applications;

·       This determines a value per point (EUR/point);

·       Each applicant receives funding according to their own score, up to the maximum of EUR 3,000.00.

The decision of the joint Evaluation Committee is final, subject to the appeal procedure set out in Article 6.

The exact amount of funding and its composition awarded to each applicant will be published via the Learning Management System OpenOLAT. This publication constitutes as notification.
description:
Purpose, amount and duration of the DIGISOC Scholarship

The University of Innsbruck is issuing a Call for Application within the DIGISOC Scholarship Programme, reserved for students enrolled for the Academic Year 2026/2027 in the second year of the Joint Master’s Programme in Digital Society, Social Innovation and Global Citizenship (DIGISOC).

The Call for Application has a total budget of EUR 50.000.

The DIGISOC Scholarship Programme is designed to provide financial support to students participating in the DIGISOC Joint Master’s Programme (JMP) and aims to:

·       Alleviate costs associated with tuition fees, summer schools, short-term mobilities, and living expenses;

·       Support students from underprivileged or vulnerable backgrounds;

·       Promote diversity, fairness, and gender balance in higher education.

The scholarship also functions as a form of social support, helping students overcome personal or socio-economic obstacles that hinder participation in international education.

The DIGISOC Scholarship is limited to one academic year and is paid out in one instalment. There is no automatic entitlement to a scholarship and no automatic renewal.

The amount of the scholarship can reach a maximum of EUR 3,000.00 gross per academic year and applicant. The exact amount assigned to each applicant is based on the points awarded in the evaluation process (see Article 5 – Awarding Criteria and Evaluation Procedure).

A maximum of 30 points can be awarded to each application. The maximum total funding per student is EUR 6,000.00 over the course of the two-year programme.

For the entire academic year for which the scholarship is awarded, the scholarship holder must not have an employment relationship with the University of Innsbruck. 

Applicants and scholarship holders are solely responsible for clarifying and complying with all tax obligations and any other individual tax consequences arising from receipt of the scholarship. The University of Innsbruck does not provide individual tax advice.

furtherInformation:
Acceptance and Appeals

Applicants are notified of decisions within 15 days after the end of the submission period via e-mail. Rejected applications include a short justification.

Applicants who are not awarded a scholarship have the right to appeal. Appeals may be submitted by e-mail to digisoc@uibk.ac.at and will be reviewed by the joint Evaluation Committee, including the designated representative responsible for disability, inclusion and/or equal-treatment matters.

Within the mandatory deadline of 5 days from receipt of the scholarship award notice, the applicant must send the declaration of acceptance by e-mail to digisoc@uibk.ac.at without reservation and under the conditions of this Call for Application. Failure to do so results in forfeiture of the award.

With the declaration of acceptance, the scholarship holder must also undertake to communicate any change occurring during the academic year that affects information previously declared or eligibility for the scholarship.


Requirements for receiving the scholarship

Before disbursement, the scholarship holder will complete the required scholarship documentation with the University of Innsbruck and must provide:

·       A current enrolment certificate showing the register number;

·       The applicant’s full residential address (street and house number, postal code, city, and country);

·       Bank details for an account held in the scholarship holder’s name, including an IBAN and any further information required to enable a SEPA credit transfer. It must be expressly possible to make the scholarship payment by SEPA transfer to the account provided;

·       A copy of a valid passport or other accepted identification document.

Scholarship holders remain solely responsible for all tax-law clarifications and obligations connected with the scholarship.

The scholarship holder must also confirm that no employment relationship with the University of Innsbruck exists or will exist for the duration of the academic year for which the scholarship is awarded.


Financial and Disbursement Procedures

Scholarships are paid in one instalment per academic year. 

Disbursement is handled by the University of Innsbruck as the DIGISOC degree-awarding university issuing this Call for Application.

Payment will be made by SEPA credit transfer to a current account in the name of the scholarship holder. The account provided must be capable of receiving a SEPA transfer. The scholarship holder is responsible for providing complete and correct bank details and for any bank charges or conversion costs that may arise outside the scope of the SEPA payment.


Renunciation

In the event of withdrawal from the scholarship after acceptance, scholarship holders must give written notice by e-mail to digisoc@uibk.ac.at.

In case of transfer to another programme during the 2026/2027 academic year, the scholarship holder will be considered to have renounced the scholarship and must return the full amount of the scholarship.

A scholarship holder who renounces the scholarship is required to return any amounts received, except in duly justified special cases, which will be assessed by the joint Evaluation Committee.


Final provisions

All resources and updates will be made available via the DIGISOC website – Costs and Scholarships page https://digitalsociety4innovation.eu/costs-and-scholarships/

The following templates and tools will be published on the same page:

·       Application and documentation guidelines;
